name: 01_basics_callback_flow.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Basics Callback Flow
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Start here: learn when OnInitialize, OnPreLayout, and OnLayout run, and
why every frame must be calculated directly from ctx.time.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Correct: closed-form function of ctx.time, safe to evaluate for any
    -- frame in any order.
    ctx.global.rotation = ctx.time * 20.0

    -- Wrong (left commented out on purpose): this looks like "advance by 1
    -- degree per frame", but ctx.global.rotation is rebuilt from the host
    -- inspector value on every call, so it never accumulates.
    -- ctx.global.rotation = ctx.global.rotation + 1.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- ctx.global.rotation here is the CONFIRMED value from OnPreLayout
    -- above (read-only at this point), not the raw inspector value.
    -- print("confirmed global rotation =", ctx.global.rotation)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        -- Also a pure function of (ctx.time, index): scrubbing backward or
        -- rendering frames out of order reproduces the exact same motion.
        character.rotation = math.sin(ctx.time * 2.0 + index * 0.2) * 15.0
    end
end
description:
Start here: learn when OnInitialize, OnPreLayout, and OnLayout run, and
why every frame must be calculated directly from ctx.time.
title: Basics Callback Flow
author: Mug

name: 02_mt_storage.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title MT Storage
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
-- @covers mt.storage
--[[ @description
Build reusable constants in OnInitialize with mt.storage, then read them
from later callbacks without keeping frame-to-frame state.
]]

function OnInitialize(ctx)
    -- Count-independent constants are fine in storage.
    mt.storage.amplitude = 0.06
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Prefer instance_seed + mt.random*: closed-form, survives text growth, and
    -- differs across instances of the same script (a fixed literal seed would
    -- repeat the same pattern on every instance).
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local phase = mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(ctx.time * 2.0 + phase) * mt.storage.amplitude
        character.rotation = math.sin(ctx.time * 1.5 + phase) * 4.0
    end

    -- Writing to mt.storage outside OnInitialize raises a Lua error;
    -- uncomment to verify.
    -- mt.storage.amplitude = 0.0
end
description:
Build reusable constants in OnInitialize with mt.storage, then read them
from later callbacks without keeping frame-to-frame state.
title: MT Storage
author: Mug

name: 03_mt_timeline.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 3
-- @title MT Timeline
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
-- @covers mt.timeline.progress mt.timeline.remaining mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds
--[[ @description
Choose clip-relative progress for whole-span motion, or real seconds for
fixed-speed intros and outros. Demonstrates all current mt.timeline helpers.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- ctx.timeline fields, all clip-local (clip start is always frame/time 0).
    -- print("available", ctx.timeline.available)
    -- print("start_frame/end_frame", ctx.timeline.start_frame, ctx.timeline.end_frame)
    -- print("duration_seconds", ctx.timeline.duration_seconds)
    -- print("progress (0..1)", ctx.timeline.progress)

    -- available is false when the host cannot resolve a finite clip range
    -- (for example scripting in isolation); the other fields fall back to 0
    -- in that case, so always guard clip-length-dependent logic with it.

    -- Whole-span motion (drift across the ENTIRE clip): this is the one
    -- case where clip-relative progress is correct, since the drift should
    -- take longer if the clip is longer. Base values (ctx.global) can only
    -- be written here, in OnPreLayout.
    local sweepProgress = mt.timeline.progress(ctx)
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5 + (sweepProgress - 0.5) * 0.1
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- WRONG for a fixed-speed reveal: typing speed changes with clip length.
    -- local visible = math.floor(mt.timeline.progress(ctx) * ctx.char_count)

    -- RIGHT: constant 0.12s per character regardless of clip length.
    local secondsPerCharacter = 0.12
    local visibleCount = math.floor(ctx.time / secondsPerCharacter)

    -- Intro anchored to clip start, outro anchored to clip end, both at a
    -- fixed real-time speed (auto-compressed only if the clip is shorter
    -- than introSeconds + outroSeconds). ctx.global is read-only by this
    -- point, so the fade is applied per-character instead.
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, 0.6, 0.6)
    local introOutroFade = mt.ease.out_cubic(introProgress) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroProgress))

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        character.opacity = introOutroFade
        if index > visibleCount then
            character.opacity = 0.0
        end
    end

    -- Outro fade over the last 0.4s of the clip, anchored to the clip end --
    -- built from mt.timeline.remaining directly, for cases that need only
    -- the outro half.
    local outroFade = mt.clamp(mt.timeline.remaining(ctx) / 0.4, 0.0, 1.0)
    -- ctx.chars[1].scale = 1.0 - (1.0 - outroFade) * 0.2
end
description:
Choose clip-relative progress for whole-span motion, or real seconds for
fixed-speed intros and outros. Demonstrates all current mt.timeline helpers.
title: MT Timeline
author: Mug

name: 04_global.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Global
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Use ctx.global in OnPreLayout to control the whole text block. Transform,
fill, gradient, stroke, and shadow are grouped for easy experimentation.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Transform: position is 0..1 canvas fraction, rotation/yaw/pitch in
    -- degrees, pivot is the point transforms are applied around.
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.1) * 0.05
    ctx.global.position_y = 0.5
    ctx.global.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 10.0
    -- ctx.global.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.1) * 15.0 -- 3D preset only
    -- ctx.global.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.13) * 10.0 -- 3D preset only
    ctx.global.scale = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.25) * 0.1
    ctx.global.stretch_x = 1.0
    ctx.global.stretch_y = 1.0
    ctx.global.pivot_x = 0.5
    ctx.global.pivot_y = 0.5
    -- Opacity multiplies with the character and part opacity below and
    -- applies to fill, gradient, stroke, shadow, and the bounding box alike.
    ctx.global.opacity = 0.5 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.15)) * 0.5

    -- Fill color and optional gradient overlay; the gradient angle spins.
    ctx.global.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    -- ctx.global.fill.transparent = true -- keep stroke/shadow, hide fill
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab" -- "none" disables the gradient
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = { r = 0.2, g = 0.6, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.gradient.midpoint = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 0.3
    ctx.global.gradient.angle = ctx.time * 30.0
    ctx.global.gradient.start_position = 0.0
    ctx.global.gradient.end_position = 1.0

    -- Stroke outline, pulsing width.
    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.01 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.02
    ctx.global.stroke.gap = 0.0
    ctx.global.stroke.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.stroke.order = "stroke_over_fill" -- or "fill_over_stroke"
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"
    ctx.global.stroke.miter_limit = 4.0

    -- Drop shadow, sweeping angle.
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.5 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2)) * 2.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = ctx.time * 60.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.5 }
end
description:
Use ctx.global in OnPreLayout to control the whole text block. Transform,
fill, gradient, stroke, and shadow are grouped for easy experimentation.
title: Global
author: Mug

name: 05_camera.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Camera
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Control the 3D camera from OnPreLayout. Enable 3D Projection to compare
target, yaw, pitch, perspective, zoom, and lens shift.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Target: the point the camera looks at, in host-normalized
    -- coordinates. Y grows upward.
    ctx.camera.target_x = 0.5
    ctx.camera.target_y = 0.5

    -- Orbit angles in degrees, sweeping back and forth.
    ctx.camera.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.1) * 25.0
    ctx.camera.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.07, math.pi / 2.0) * 12.0

    -- Perspective strength: higher values exaggerate depth.
    ctx.camera.perspective = 0.55 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.08) * 0.25

    -- Zoom multiplier: higher values move the camera closer.
    ctx.camera.zoom = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.12) * 0.1

    -- Lens shift: principal-point offset as a canvas fraction, independent
    -- of the orbit angles. Y grows upward.
    ctx.camera.lens_shift_x = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.06) * 0.03
    ctx.camera.lens_shift_y = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.09, math.pi / 2.0) * 0.02
end
description:
Control the 3D camera from OnPreLayout. Enable 3D Projection to compare
target, yaw, pitch, perspective, zoom, and lens shift.
title: Camera
author: Mug

name: 06_character.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Character
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Read and modify individual characters through ctx.chars in OnLayout.
The second character is isolated so each transform and style is easy to see.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < 2 then
        return
    end

    local character = ctx.chars[2]

    -- Read-only identity and geometry.
    -- print(character.index, character.text, character.line_index)
    -- print(character.geometry.bounds_center_x, character.geometry.bounds_center_y)

    -- Transform: offset is 0.5-centered (0.5 = no displacement), pivot is
    -- the point rotation/scale are applied around, in host-normalized
    -- coordinates. Y grows upward.
    character.offset_x = 0.5
    character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.5) * 0.08
    character.pivot_x = 0.5
    character.pivot_y = 0.5
    character.scale = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.4) * 0.3
    character.stretch_x = 1.0
    character.stretch_y = 1.0
    character.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3) * 20.0
    -- character.z = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 0.3 -- 3D preset only
    -- character.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 20.0 -- 3D preset only
    -- character.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.25) * 10.0 -- 3D preset only
    -- Opacity multiplies with ctx.global.opacity and the owning parts' opacity.
    character.opacity = 0.4 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.6)) * 0.6

    -- Per-character fill overrides the global fill only while fill.use
    -- is true; hue cycles over time.
    character.fill.use = true
    character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0), 0.8, 1.0, 1.0)

    -- Per-character stroke overrides the global stroke width/gap/color
    -- only while stroke.use is true.
    -- character.stroke.use = true
    -- character.stroke.width = 0.01 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.02
    -- character.stroke.gap = 0.0
    -- character.stroke.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }

    -- Per-character shadow color overrides the global shadow color only
    -- while shadow.use is true.
    -- character.shadow.use = true
    -- character.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.3, a = 0.6 }
end
description:
Read and modify individual characters through ctx.chars in OnLayout.
The second character is isolated so each transform and style is easy to see.
title: Character
author: Mug

name: 07_part.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "%=%"
-- @title Part
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Find and style glyph parts through ctx.parts. The recommended text makes
character ownership and per-character part indices easy to compare.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]

        -- character_index identifies the owner; index_in_character restarts
        -- from 1 for every character.
        local owner = ctx.chars[part.character_index]
        local phase = part.index_in_character * 0.8 + part.character_index * 0.3
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.5, phase) * 0.04
        part.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.35, phase) * 12.0

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(
            mt.wrap(part.character_index * 0.2 + part.index_in_character * 0.08, 0.0, 1.0),
            0.7,
            1.0
        )

        -- The owning character exposes its contiguous range in ctx.parts.
        local belongsToOwner =
            index >= owner.part_start and index < owner.part_start + owner.part_count
        assert(belongsToOwner, "part ownership range is inconsistent")
    end
end
description:
Find and style glyph parts through ctx.parts. The recommended text makes
character ownership and per-character part indices easy to compare.
title: Part
author: Mug

name: 08_inheritance.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6
-- @title Inheritance
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
See style inheritance from global to character to part. Toggle each `use`
flag to compare inherited and explicitly overridden values.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Global fill is white, but the gradient overlay repaints anything that
    -- is not using an individual color.
    ctx.global.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab"
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = { r = 0.2, g = 0.6, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Character 1: fill.use toggles on a slow square wave. While it is
    -- false, this character is painted by the gradient like the rest of
    -- the untouched text; the instant it flips to true, a flat red wins
    -- over the gradient entirely.
    if ctx.char_count >= 1 then
        local character = ctx.chars[1]
        character.fill.use = mt.wave_square(ctx.time, 0.2) > 0.0
        character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.2, b = 0.2, a = 1.0 }
    end

    -- Character 2: fill.use stays true throughout, but the flat color
    -- itself cycles hue -- contrast this with character 1's on/off flip.
    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        local character = ctx.chars[2]
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0), 0.8, 1.0)
    end

    -- Character 3, part 1: the character's OWN fill.use stays false
    -- (inherits Global/gradient throughout), but the first owned part
    -- toggles fill.use on its own square wave -- out of phase with
    -- character 1 -- so only that one part ever differs from its
    -- character, and only while its own toggle is on.
    if ctx.char_count >= 3 and ctx.part_count >= 1 then
        local character = ctx.chars[3]
        if character.part_count >= 1 then
            local part = ctx.parts[character.part_start]
            part.fill.use = mt.wave_square(ctx.time, 0.2, math.pi) > 0.0
            part.fill.color = { r = 0.2, g = 1.0, b = 0.4, a = 1.0 }
        end
    end

    -- Shadow color follows the exact same chain as fill: a character's
    -- resolved shadow.color propagates down to its owned parts unless a
    -- part sets shadow.use = true itself.
    -- ctx.chars[1].shadow.use = true
    -- ctx.chars[1].shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.6 }
end
description:
See style inheritance from global to character to part. Toggle each `use`
flag to compare inherited and explicitly overridden values.
title: Inheritance
author: Mug

name: 09_bounding_box.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Bounding Box
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Draw and animate the text frame through ctx.bounding_box in OnLayout.
This is independent from the write-on and draw-order controls in ctx.output.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- The box outline itself, all 4 edges drawn with rounded caps.
    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = true
    ctx.bounding_box.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.bounding_box.start_cap = "round" -- see MtBoundingBox for valid caps
    ctx.bounding_box.end_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.corner_radius = 1.0

    -- Outline width pulses so the stroke's own animation is unambiguous.
    ctx.bounding_box.width = 3.0 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.25)) * 6.0

    -- Margin between the text and the box breathes in and out, so the box
    -- itself visibly grows/shrinks around the (otherwise static) text.
    local margin = 2.0 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2)) * 8.0
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = margin
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = margin

    -- Fill behind the text, independent of the outline; opacity cycles.
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = 0.15 + mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.3

    -- Fill and stroke can be nudged independently of each other and of the
    -- text/margin above (for a detached-shadow-like offset look).
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_offset_x = 0.0
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_offset_y = 0.0
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_x = 0.0
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_y = 0.0
end
description:
Draw and animate the text frame through ctx.bounding_box in OnLayout.
This is independent from the write-on and draw-order controls in ctx.output.
title: Bounding Box
author: Mug

name: 10_output.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Output
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Use ctx.output in OnLayout for write-on animation, filtering, and draw order.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- Write-on reveal range, normalized 0.0..1.0 across the whole sequence.
    -- write_on_mode selects whether that range advances through characters
    -- or parts. Here the reveal sweeps forward and back on a 4-second
    -- cycle, so characters visibly appear and disappear in text order.
    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "character" -- or "part"
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 4.0)

    -- Manual reveal and draw order overrides the natural text order; see
    -- MtOutput for the manual_order_text syntax. Uncomment to reveal
    -- characters 3, then 1, then 2 instead of left-to-right.
    -- ctx.output.manual_order_enabled = true
    -- ctx.output.manual_order_text = "3,1,2"

    -- reorder_parts affects only multi-part characters (for example CJK
    -- strokes or symbols like "%"/"="), so it has no visible effect on
    -- plain single-part Latin text.
    -- ctx.output.reorder_parts = true
end
description: Use ctx.output in OnLayout for write-on animation, filtering, and draw order.
title: Output
author: Mug

name: 11_layout_shaping.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 12
-- @title Layout Shaping
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Change text shaping before layout: text, tracking, line spacing, writing
direction, alignment, and per-character margins.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Text and font can be reassigned; font_name must be one of ctx.fonts.
    ctx.global.text = "Line one\nLine two\nLine three"
    -- ctx.global.font_name = ctx.fonts[1]

    -- Extra spacing added between characters, breathing in and out.
    ctx.global.tracking = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.2) * 0.06

    -- Multiplies the distance between lines.
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.0 + mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.15) * 0.4

    -- Switches to vertical (top-to-bottom) writing.
    -- ctx.global.vertical = true

    -- Horizontal alignment: "left" | "center" | "right". Cycled on a
    -- 3-second step so each value is visibly held, not blended.
    local horizontalAlignments = { "left", "center", "right" }
    local horizontalStep = math.floor(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0) * #horizontalAlignments) + 1
    ctx.global.h_align = horizontalAlignments[horizontalStep]

    -- Vertical alignment: "top" | "center" | "bottom" | "baseline". Cycled
    -- independently on its own 4-second step.
    local verticalAlignments = { "top", "center", "bottom", "baseline" }
    local verticalStep = math.floor(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 4.0) * #verticalAlignments) + 1
    ctx.global.v_align = verticalAlignments[verticalStep]

    -- Per-character extra margin, indexed from 1. Missing indices default
    -- to zero, so a short table only affects the first characters. Here
    -- the margin before the second character pulses over time.
    ctx.global.margins = { 0.0, mt.saturate(mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.3)) * 0.12 }
end
description:
Change text shaping before layout: text, tracking, line spacing, writing
direction, alignment, and per-character margins.
title: Layout Shaping
author: Mug

name: 12_mt_color.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title MT Color
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
-- @covers mt.color.lerp mt.color.from_hsv mt.color.with_alpha mt.color.from_oklch
--[[ @description
Create, fade, and interpolate colors with mt.color. Every helper returns a
new color table and leaves its inputs unchanged.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    -- from_hsv builds an RGBA color from normalized hue/saturation/value.
    local hueColor = mt.color.from_hsv(0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.0)

    -- from_oklch builds an RGBA color from the perceptually-uniform OKLCH
    -- space (lightness, chroma, hue); useful when interpolating hues needs
    -- to look perceptually even, unlike raw HSV interpolation.
    local oklchColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.75, 0.15, 0.6, 1.0)

    -- lerp interpolates two RGBA color tables component-wise.
    local red = { r = 1.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
    local blue = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    local mixed = mt.color.lerp(red, blue, 0.5)

    -- with_alpha copies a color while replacing only its alpha channel.
    local translucentRed = mt.color.with_alpha(red, 0.4)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local hue = mt.distribute(index, ctx.char_count)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(hue, 0.75, 1.0, 1.0)
    end

    -- Uncomment to inspect the constructed colors directly.
    -- print(hueColor.r, hueColor.g, hueColor.b, hueColor.a)
    -- print(oklchColor.r, oklchColor.g, oklchColor.b)
    -- print(mixed.r, mixed.g, mixed.b)
    -- print(translucentRed.a)
end
description:
Create, fade, and interpolate colors with mt.color. Every helper returns a
new color table and leaves its inputs unchanged.
title: MT Color
author: Mug

name: 13_mt_values.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "VALUES"
-- @title MT Values
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
-- @covers mt.clamp mt.saturate mt.lerp mt.inverse_lerp mt.remap mt.wrap
-- @covers mt.lerp_angle mt.distribute mt.smoothstep mt.cycle mt.pingpong
--[[ @description
Normalize, remap, interpolate, and repeat values with the core mt helpers.
Each result drives a visible character property.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local progress = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 2.0)
    local eased = mt.smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, progress)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local position = mt.distribute(index, ctx.char_count)

        -- remap converts the 0..1 character position into a canvas offset;
        -- inverse_lerp converts that result back to normalized progress.
        local horizontal = mt.remap(position, 0.0, 1.0, -0.08, 0.08, true)
        local recovered = mt.inverse_lerp(-0.08, 0.08, horizontal)
        character.offset_x = 0.5 + horizontal
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.lerp(-0.06, 0.06, eased)
        character.scale = 0.8 + mt.saturate(recovered) * 0.4

        -- lerp_angle takes the short route across the 0/360-degree seam.
        character.rotation = mt.lerp_angle(350.0, 10.0, progress)
        character.opacity = mt.clamp(0.35 + eased, 0.0, 1.0)

        -- cycle repeats in 0..1; wrap keeps the added hue in the same range.
        local hue = mt.wrap(mt.cycle(ctx.time, 3.0) + position, 0.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(hue, 0.7, 1.0)
    end
end
description:
Normalize, remap, interpolate, and repeat values with the core mt helpers.
Each result drives a visible character property.
title: MT Values

--[[ @description
Use deterministic random values for stable variation and noise for smooth
time-varying motion. Both are safe during scrubbing and parallel rendering.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]

        -- Same seed and index always produce the same values.
        local stableScale = mt.random(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index)
        local stableRotation =
            mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed + 1, index, -8.0, 8.0)
        character.scale = 0.85 + stableScale * 0.3
        character.rotation = stableRotation

        -- Move the sample position with time for continuous motion.
        local oneDimensionalNoise =
            mt.noise1(ctx.time * 1.5 + index * 0.4, ctx.meta.instance_seed)
        local twoDimensionalNoise =
            mt.noise2(ctx.time, index * 0.3, ctx.meta.instance_seed + 2)
        character.offset_x =
            0.5 + oneDimensionalNoise * character.geometry.advance_x * 0.2
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + twoDimensionalNoise * 0.03
    end
end

-- @covers mt.ease.in_cubic mt.ease.out_cubic mt.ease.in_out_cubic

-- @covers mt.ease.cubic_bezier
--[[ @description
Compare every easing curve with the same 0–1 input. Each character uses the
corresponding function in the table below.

local kEasingFunctions = {
    mt.ease.linear,
    mt.ease.in_quad, mt.ease.out_quad, mt.ease.in_out_quad,
    mt.ease.in_cubic, mt.ease.out_cubic, mt.ease.in_out_cubic,
    mt.ease.in_quart, mt.ease.out_quart, mt.ease.in_out_quart,
    mt.ease.in_sine, mt.ease.out_sine, mt.ease.in_out_sine,
    mt.ease.in_circ, mt.ease.out_circ, mt.ease.in_out_circ,
    mt.ease.in_expo, mt.ease.out_expo, mt.ease.in_out_expo,
    mt.ease.in_back, mt.ease.out_back, mt.ease.in_out_back,
    mt.ease.in_elastic, mt.ease.out_elastic, mt.ease.in_out_elastic,
    mt.ease.in_bounce, mt.ease.out_bounce, mt.ease.in_out_bounce,
    function(progress)
        return mt.ease.cubic_bezier(0.42, 0.0, 0.58, 1.0, progress)
    end,
}

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local progress = mt.pingpong(ctx.time, 2.0)
    for index, evaluate in ipairs(kEasingFunctions) do
        if index <= ctx.char_count then
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            character.offset_y = 0.4 + evaluate(progress) * 0.2

end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- @title MT Keyframes
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
-- @covers mt.keyframes
--[[ @description
Build a multi-pose animation with mt.keyframes. Numeric and color values are
interpolated directly from the current time without stored state.
]]

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < 1 then
        return
    end

    -- Numeric keyframes: fall in with a bounce, hold, then ease out.
    -- Looped over a repeating window so the whole sequence replays.
    local loopedTime = ctx.time % 2.0
    local keyframedOffset = mt.keyframes({
        { t = 0.0, v = -0.15 },
        { t = 0.3, v = 0.0, ease = "out_bounce" },
        { t = 1.2, v = 0.0 },
        { t = 1.6, v = -0.15, ease = "in_cubic" },
    }, loopedTime)
    ctx.chars[1].offset_y = 0.5 + keyframedOffset

    -- Color keyframes: the same function interpolates { r, g, b, a } tables
    -- directly -- no separate color-specific keyframe helper needed. A
    -- single `keys` array must be all-number or all-color, never mixed.
    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        local tint = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 } },
            { t = 1.0, v = { r = 1.0, g = 0.4, b = 0.1, a = 1.0 }, ease = "out_cubic" },
            { t = 2.0, v = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }, ease = "in_cubic" },
        }, loopedTime)
        ctx.chars[2].fill.use = true
        ctx.chars[2].fill.color = tint
    end
end
description:
Build a multi-pose animation with mt.keyframes. Numeric and color values are
interpolated directly from the current time without stored state.

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- @title MT Layout Reflow
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 2
-- @covers mt.layout.reflow
--[[ @description
Restore spacing and baseline alignment after per-character scale or stretch.
Call mt.layout.reflow as the final layout operation for the frame.
]]

local kAnchorIndex = 1

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < kAnchorIndex then
        return
    end

    -- reflow preserves the anchor's current transformed typesetting origin.
    -- Put its scale pivot on the horizontal baseline so the anchor itself
    -- cannot move the whole line vertically while its scale changes.
    local anchor = ctx.chars[kAnchorIndex]
    anchor.pivot_y = 0.5
        + anchor.geometry.canvas_origin_y
        - anchor.geometry.bounds_center_y

    -- Pass 1: any per-character size animation. Left alone, scaling around
    -- each character's own natural center would drift the baseline and
    -- crowd/gap the neighbors.
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        character.scale = 0.6 + 0.4 * mt.stagger(ctx.time % 2.0, index, 0.1, 0.5)
    end

    -- Pass 2: re-typeset the whole line using scaled font advances and a
    -- small extra gap (as a fraction of canvas width). This does not
    -- equalize the visible ink gap between unlike glyph shapes.
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.01, { anchor = kAnchorIndex })
end
description:
Restore spacing and baseline alignment after per-character scale or stretch.
Call mt.layout.reflow as the final layout operation for the frame.
title: MT Layout Reflow
author: Mug

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "ABCDEFGH"
-- @title MT Layout Reflow Comparison
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 1
--[[ @description
Compare partial scaling without reflow against corrected spacing. Red characters
shrink, separate, reflow, overlap while growing, then reflow again.
]]

local kTargetIndices = { 3, 4, 5, 6 }
local kAnchorIndex = 3
local kShrunkScale = 0.55
local kFullScale = 1.0

local kHoldFullEnd = 0.5
local kShrinkEnd = 1.5
local kHoldShrunkEnd = 2.0
local kAlignShrunkEnd = 2.5
local kGrowOverlapEnd = 3.5
local kHoldOverlapEnd = 4.0
local kAlignFullEnd = 4.5

local function applyScale(ctx, scale)
    for _, index in ipairs(kTargetIndices) do
        if index <= ctx.char_count then
            ctx.chars[index].scale = scale
        end
    end
end

-- Reflow at one scale, then restore another scale for display. This makes
-- the overlap caused by growing beyond the packed layout easy to see.
local function reflowAtScale(ctx, layoutScale, displayScale)
    applyScale(ctx, layoutScale)
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, {
        targets = kTargetIndices,
        anchor = kAnchorIndex,
    })
    applyScale(ctx, displayScale)
end

local function colorCharacters(ctx)
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local isTarget =
            index >= kTargetIndices[1]
            and index <= kTargetIndices[#kTargetIndices]
        character.fill.use = true
        if isTarget then
            character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.35, b = 0.35, a = 1.0 }
        else
            character.fill.color = { r = 0.6, g = 0.6, b = 0.6, a = 1.0 }
        end
    end
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    colorCharacters(ctx)

    if ctx.time < kHoldFullEnd then
        applyScale(ctx, kFullScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kShrinkEnd then
        local progress = mt.smoothstep(kHoldFullEnd, kShrinkEnd, ctx.time)
        applyScale(ctx, mt.lerp(kFullScale, kShrunkScale, progress))
    elseif ctx.time < kHoldShrunkEnd then
        -- No reflow: each character shrinks around its own center, leaving gaps.
        applyScale(ctx, kShrunkScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kAlignShrunkEnd then
        -- Reflow closes the gaps while character 3 remains anchored.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kShrunkScale, kShrunkScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kGrowOverlapEnd then
        local progress = mt.smoothstep(kAlignShrunkEnd, kGrowOverlapEnd, ctx.time)
        local displayScale = mt.lerp(kShrunkScale, kFullScale, progress)
        -- Keep the packed positions while growing to reveal the overlap.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kShrunkScale, displayScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kHoldOverlapEnd then
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kShrunkScale, kFullScale)
    elseif ctx.time < kAlignFullEnd then
        -- Reflow at full scale resolves the overlap.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kFullScale, kFullScale)
    else
        -- Reflow must run every frame; layout changes are not persistent.
        reflowAtScale(ctx, kFullScale, kFullScale)
    end
end
description:
Compare partial scaling without reflow against corrected spacing. Red characters
shrink, separate, reflow, overlap while growing, then reflow again.
title: MT Layout Reflow Comparison
author: Mug

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "OOOOOOOO++++++++"
-- @title MT Aspect Ratio Correction
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
-- @covers mt.falloff mt.polar_offset mt.friction_decay mt.layout.radial_distance
--[[ @description
Compare an uncorrected normalized circle with an aspect-corrected circle.
Only the corrected path keeps a constant physical radius.
]]

local kMarkersPerCircle = 8
local kRadius = 0.12
local kRawCenterX = 0.28
local kCorrectedCenterX = 0.72
local kCenterY = 0.5

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local rotation = mt.friction_decay(ctx.time, 90.0, 0.8)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local groupIndex = math.floor((index - 1) / kMarkersPerCircle) + 1
        local markerIndex = (index - 1) % kMarkersPerCircle + 1
        local isCorrected = groupIndex == 2
        local centerX = isCorrected and kCorrectedCenterX or kRawCenterX
        local angle =
            mt.distribute(markerIndex, kMarkersPerCircle) * 360.0 + rotation
        local offsetX, offsetY = mt.polar_offset(angle, kRadius)

        -- Equal normalized X/Y offsets form a wide ellipse on a wide canvas.
        -- Dividing X by width/height restores equal physical radii.
        local correctedOffsetX =
            isCorrected and offsetX / ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio or offsetX
        local targetX = centerX + correctedOffsetX
        local targetY = kCenterY - offsetY

        local physicalRadius =
            mt.layout.radial_distance(ctx, targetX, targetY, centerX, kCenterY)
        local radiusAccuracy =
            mt.falloff(math.abs(physicalRadius - kRadius), 0.025)

        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        character.scale = 0.35 + radiusAccuracy * 0.25
        character.opacity = 0.35 + radiusAccuracy * 0.65
        character.fill.use = true
        if isCorrected then
            character.fill.color = { r = 0.1, g = 0.75, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
        else
            character.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 0.35, b = 0.1, a = 1.0 }
        end
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, targetX, targetY)
    end
end
description:
Compare an uncorrected normalized circle with an aspect-corrected circle.
Only the corrected path keeps a constant physical radius.
title: MT Aspect Ratio Correction
author: Mug

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "ABC"
-- @title MT Layout Position
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
-- @covers mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d mt.layout.canvas_to_offset_2d mt.layout.place_2d
--[[ @description
Place characters and parts at exact canvas positions through transformed
hierarchies. Shows the calculation API and its mutating convenience wrapper.
]]

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- A non-identity parent transform makes direct offset assignment incorrect.
    ctx.global.rotation = 12.0
    ctx.global.scale = 0.9
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local phase = ctx.time * 1.5
    local targetX = 0.5 + math.cos(phase) * 0.18
    local targetY = 0.5 + math.sin(phase) * 0.12

    if ctx.char_count >= 1 then
        local character = ctx.chars[1]
        -- Calculate offsets without mutation, then apply both components.
        local offsetX, offsetY =
            mt.layout.canvas_to_offset_2d(ctx, character, targetX, targetY)
        character.offset_x = offsetX
        character.offset_y = offsetY

        local actualX, actualY = mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d(ctx, character)
        character.opacity = 1.0 - math.min(math.abs(actualX - targetX) + math.abs(actualY - targetY), 1.0)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 2 then
        -- place_2d performs the same calculation and writes the offsets.
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, ctx.chars[2], 1.0 - targetX, targetY)
    end

    if ctx.char_count >= 3 and ctx.chars[3].part_count > 0 then
        -- The same API handles a part through its owning-character hierarchy.
        local part = ctx.parts[ctx.chars[3].part_start]
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, part, 0.5, 1.0 - targetY)
    end
end
description:
Place characters and parts at exact canvas positions through transformed
hierarchies. Shows the calculation API and its mutating convenience wrapper.

name: 25_mt_layout_bounds.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend text "MW+++++"
-- @title MT Layout Bounds
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 2
-- @covers mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d
--[[ @description
Measure transformed 2D bounds. Four orange markers follow the corners, while
the yellow marker follows the center.
]]

local kCharacterTargets = { 1, 2 }
local kFirstMarkerIndex = 3
local kMarkerCount = 5
local kComparisonTolerance = 0.000001
local kCycleSeconds = 5.0

local function assertClose(actual, expected, message)
    assert(math.abs(actual - expected) <= kComparisonTolerance, message)
end

local function collectOwnedParts(ctx)
    local targets = {}
    for partIndex = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[partIndex]
        if part.character_index == 1 or part.character_index == 2 then
            table.insert(targets, partIndex)
        end
    end
    return targets
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local angle = ctx.time / kCycleSeconds * math.pi * 2.0
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5
    ctx.global.position_y = 0.5
    ctx.global.pivot_x = 0.5
    ctx.global.pivot_y = 0.5
    ctx.global.rotation = 8.0 * math.sin(angle)
    ctx.global.scale = 0.9
    ctx.global.stretch_x = 1.05
    ctx.global.stretch_y = 0.95
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < kFirstMarkerIndex + kMarkerCount - 1 then
        return
    end

    local angle = ctx.time / kCycleSeconds * math.pi * 2.0
    local firstCharacter = ctx.chars[1]
    local secondCharacter = ctx.chars[2]

    firstCharacter.scale = 1.15 + 0.25 * math.sin(angle)
    firstCharacter.stretch_x = 1.2
    firstCharacter.stretch_y = 0.8
    firstCharacter.rotation = 28.0 * math.sin(angle)
    firstCharacter.pivot_x = 0.58
    firstCharacter.pivot_y = 0.43

    secondCharacter.scale = 1.0 + 0.2 * math.cos(angle)
    secondCharacter.stretch_x = 0.75
    secondCharacter.stretch_y = 1.25
    secondCharacter.rotation = -34.0 * math.cos(angle)
    secondCharacter.pivot_x = 0.42
    secondCharacter.pivot_y = 0.57

    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, firstCharacter, 0.4, 0.52)
    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, secondCharacter, 0.6, 0.48)

    firstCharacter.fill.use = true
    firstCharacter.fill.color = { r = 0.15, g = 0.55, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    secondCharacter.fill.use = true
    secondCharacter.fill.color = { r = 0.15, g = 0.8, b = 0.95, a = 1.0 }

    -- Omitting targetType selects character indices.
    local characterBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, kCharacterTargets)
    assert(characterBounds ~= nil, "character bounds must be measurable")

    -- The explicit "part" form accepts global part indices.
    local partTargets = collectOwnedParts(ctx)
    local partBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, partTargets, "part")
    assert(partBounds ~= nil, "part bounds must be measurable")
    assertClose(partBounds.left, characterBounds.left, "part/character left mismatch")
    assertClose(partBounds.right, characterBounds.right, "part/character right mismatch")
    assertClose(partBounds.bottom, characterBounds.bottom, "part/character bottom mismatch")
    assertClose(partBounds.top, characterBounds.top, "part/character top mismatch")

    local markerPositions = {
        { x = characterBounds.left, y = characterBounds.top },
        { x = characterBounds.right, y = characterBounds.top },
        { x = characterBounds.right, y = characterBounds.bottom },
        { x = characterBounds.left, y = characterBounds.bottom },
        { x = characterBounds.center_x, y = characterBounds.center_y },
    }

    for markerOffset, position in ipairs(markerPositions) do
        local marker = ctx.chars[kFirstMarkerIndex + markerOffset - 1]
        local isCenterMarker = markerOffset == kMarkerCount
        marker.scale = isCenterMarker and 0.32 or 0.24
        marker.fill.use = true

-- @covers mt.path.arc_length mt.path.arc_length.length mt.path.arc_length.at_distance
-- @covers mt.layout.queue_on_path
--[[ @description
Compare path queues moving left-to-right, right-to-left, and vertically.
Each two-second phase shows the required targets, mode, and heading correction.
]]

local kConfigurations = {
    {
        points = {
            { x = 0.1, y = 0.45 }, { x = 0.35, y = 0.62 },
            { x = 0.65, y = 0.38 }, { x = 0.9, y = 0.55 },
        },
        reverseTargets = false,
        mode = "horizontal",
        headingCorrection = 0.0,
    },
    {
        points = {
            { x = 0.9, y = 0.45 }, { x = 0.65, y = 0.62 },
            { x = 0.35, y = 0.38 }, { x = 0.1, y = 0.55 },
        },
        reverseTargets = true,
        mode = "horizontal",
        headingCorrection = 180.0,
    },
    {
        points = {
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.15 }, { x = 0.65, y = 0.35 },
            { x = 0.35, y = 0.65 }, { x = 0.5, y = 0.85 },
        },
        reverseTargets = true,
        mode = "vertical",
        headingCorrection = 90.0,
    },
}

local function configurationIndex(time)
    return math.floor(time / 2.0) % #kConfigurations + 1
end

local function orderedTargets(characterCount, reverse)
    local targets = {}
    for offset = 1, characterCount do
        local index = reverse and (characterCount - offset + 1) or offset
        targets[#targets + 1] = index
    end
    return targets
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local configuration = kConfigurations[configurationIndex(ctx.time)]
    ctx.global.vertical = configuration.mode == "vertical"
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local configuration = kConfigurations[configurationIndex(ctx.time)]
    local phaseTime = ctx.time % 2.0
    local path = mt.path.arc_length(configuration.points, ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio)
    local pathLength = path:length()
    local slots = mt.layout.queue_on_path(ctx, path, {
        align = "end",
        gap = math.min(0.004, pathLength * 0.01),
        mode = configuration.mode,
        targets = orderedTargets(ctx.char_count, configuration.reverseTargets),
    })
    local sharedProgress = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(phaseTime / 1.5))

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local distanceRatio = math.min(sharedProgress, slots[index])
        local x, y, heading = path:at_distance(distanceRatio)
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        character.rotation = heading + configuration.headingCorrection
        mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, x, y)
    end
end
description:
Compare path queues moving left-to-right, right-to-left, and vertically.
Each two-second phase shows the required targets, mode, and heading correction.

name: 01_typewriter.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #1e1e1e
-- @title Typewriter
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Characters are typed at a fixed real-time
rate from the clip start via ctx.output.write_on_*, and near the clip
end they are deleted backspace-style at a slightly faster rate. Each
newly typed character also pops in with a small overshoot so the typing
edge feels mechanical rather than a flat reveal.

Both rates are real seconds (anchored to clip start / clip end), so
retiming the clip changes only how long the fully typed line holds.
]]

local kSecondsPerType = 0.09 -- typing rate, anchored to the clip start
local kSecondsPerDelete = 0.05 -- backspace rate, anchored to the clip end
local kPopDuration = 0.25 -- seconds each typed character takes to settle
local kPopScale = 0.35 -- overshoot amount at the moment a character lands
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    local typedCharacters = ctx.time / kSecondsPerType
    local keepableCharacters = remainingSeconds / kSecondsPerDelete
    local visibleCharacters =
        mt.clamp(math.min(typedCharacters, keepableCharacters), 0.0, characterCount)

    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "character"
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = visibleCharacters / characterCount

    -- Pop-in on the typing edge: scale each character by how long ago it
    -- was typed. During the backspace phase the pop is already settled,
    -- so this only shapes the entrance.
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local secondsSinceTyped = ctx.time - index * kSecondsPerType
        local settle = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(secondsSinceTyped / kPopDuration))
        character.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - settle) * kPopScale
    end
end
description:
Characters are typed at a fixed real-time
rate from the clip start via ctx.output.write_on_*, and near the clip
end they are deleted backspace-style at a slightly faster rate. Each
newly typed character also pops in with a small overshoot so the typing
edge feels mechanical rather than a flat reveal.

Both rates are real seconds (anchored to clip start / clip end), so
retiming the clip changes only how long the fully typed line holds.

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Pop Bounce
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Variety-show style characters pop in one after
another with an elastic overshoot, hold with a gentle synchronized
pulse, then shrink away in order while twisting slightly. The stagger
runs across the whole line so both the entrance and the exit read as a
left-to-right cascade.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.6 -- how much of each window is spread across characters
local kIdlePulseAmount = 0.02 -- scale amplitude of the hold-phase pulse
local kIdlePulseSpeed = 1.2 -- pulses per second during the hold
local kExitTwistDegrees = 25.0 -- rotation each character picks up while leaving

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local charIntro = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local charOutro = mt.ease.in_back(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        local idlePulse = mt.wave(ctx.time, kIdlePulseSpeed, index * 0.4) * kIdlePulseAmount

        character.scale = charIntro * (1.0 - charOutro) + idlePulse * charIntro
        character.rotation = charOutro * kExitTwistDegrees
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(charIntro * 4.0) * (1.0 - charOutro)
    end
end
description:
Variety-show style characters pop in one after
another with an elastic overshoot, hold with a gentle synchronized
pulse, then shrink away in order while twisting slightly. The stagger
runs across the whole line so both the entrance and the exit read as a
left-to-right cascade.

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Tracking Reveal
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Cinematic title reveal. The line starts letterspaced far
apart and almost transparent, converges while fading in, keeps drifting
apart very slowly during the hold (the classic movie-title tracking
creep), then spreads wide again as it fades out.

Tracking is faked with per-character offset_x: each character is pushed
away from the line center proportionally to its distance from it, so
the layout itself is never retypeset.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kIntroSpread = 0.12 -- canvas-width fraction the outermost characters start away
local kOutroSpread = 0.10 -- canvas-width fraction the outermost characters end away
local kIdleCreepPerSecond = 0.004 -- slow hold-phase tracking drift, canvas-width fraction

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local introEase = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount)
    local outroEase = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)

    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local lineCenter = (characterCount + 1) * 0.5

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        -- -1.0 at the left edge of the line, +1.0 at the right edge.
        local centerDistance = 0.0
        if characterCount > 1 then
            centerDistance = (index - lineCenter) / (lineCenter - 1.0)
        end

        local spread = (1.0 - introEase) * kIntroSpread
            + outroEase * kOutroSpread
            + ctx.time * kIdleCreepPerSecond

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + centerDistance * spread
        character.opacity = introEase * (1.0 - outroEase)
    end
end
description:
Cinematic title reveal. The line starts letterspaced far

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Part Assemble
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Every part flies in from its own
random direction with its own spin and settles into the glyph; at the
outro the parts burst apart along DIFFERENT random directions, so the
exit reads as an explosion rather than a reversed entrance.

Most Latin letters are a single part, so try this with multi-part
glyphs (kanji, kana, "%", "=") to see characters visibly self-assemble
from separate strokes.

All per-part randomness is derived from ctx.meta.instance_seed, so it
is stable across frames and differs between effect instances.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.5 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kMinScatter = 0.15 -- canvas fraction, shortest fly-in distance
local kMaxScatter = 0.35 -- canvas fraction, longest fly-in distance
local kBurstDistance = 0.45 -- canvas fraction the parts travel while bursting
local kMaxSpinDegrees = 200.0 -- fly-in spin at the fully scattered pose
local kEntryScale = 0.4 -- extra scale while scattered (parts fly in large)

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local stagger = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kStaggerAmount)
        local partIntro = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local partOutro = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        -- Independent random channels are decorrelated by salting the
        -- index with the part count.
        local inAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local outAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 2, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local scatter = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 3, kMinScatter, kMaxScatter)
        local spin = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 4, -kMaxSpinDegrees, kMaxSpinDegrees)

        local flyIn = 1.0 - partIntro
        local burst = partOutro * kBurstDistance

        part.offset_x = 0.5 + math.cos(inAngle) * scatter * flyIn + math.cos(outAngle) * burst
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(inAngle) * scatter * flyIn + math.sin(outAngle) * burst
        part.rotation = spin * flyIn + spin * partOutro
        part.scale = 1.0 + kEntryScale * flyIn
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(partIntro * 3.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(partOutro))
    end
end

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend lang ja
-- @recommend text "永字八法"
-- @title Stroke Order Draw
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Parts are revealed one by one in stroke
order (ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part" with reorder_parts), so kanji
appear to be written stroke by stroke; near the clip end the strokes
are erased in reverse order at a faster rate. Each stroke also pops
slightly as it lands.

The text is forced to kanji here because stroke order is invisible on
single-part Latin letters; swap in your own multi-part text freely.

The pop timing is approximated from the part's layout index. Inside a
multi-part character the actual reveal order is the stroke order, which
can differ from layout order, but both fall in the same time window so
the approximation is not visible.
]]

local kSecondsPerStroke = 0.14 -- drawing rate, anchored to the clip start
local kSecondsPerErase = 0.07 -- erasing rate, anchored to the clip end
local kPopDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each stroke takes to settle
local kPopScale = 0.25 -- overshoot amount at the moment a stroke lands
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local partCount = math.max(ctx.part_count, 1)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    local drawnStrokes = ctx.time / kSecondsPerStroke
    local keepableStrokes = remainingSeconds / kSecondsPerErase
    local visibleStrokes = mt.clamp(math.min(drawnStrokes, keepableStrokes), 0.0, partCount)

    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part"
    ctx.output.reorder_parts = true
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = visibleStrokes / partCount

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local secondsSinceDrawn = ctx.time - index * kSecondsPerStroke
        local settle = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(secondsSinceDrawn / kPopDuration))
        part.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - settle) * kPopScale
    end
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Part Flip 3D
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Parts start edge-on like split-flap
tiles and flip to face the camera in a left-to-right cascade, slightly
overshooting before settling; at the outro they flip over the OTHER
axis (pitch instead of yaw) while sinking away in depth, so the exit
reads as the board folding down rather than a reversed entrance.

part.yaw / part.pitch / part.z are script-only 3D fields: they can be
written under any preset, but only render with 3D Projection enabled.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.8 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kEdgeOnDegrees = 90.0 -- yaw/pitch at which a tile is edge-on (invisible)
local kSinkDepth = 0.5 -- z travelled while the board folds away

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.part_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local flipIn = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local foldOut = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        part.yaw = (1.0 - flipIn) * kEdgeOnDegrees
        part.pitch = foldOut * kEdgeOnDegrees
        part.z = foldOut * kSinkDepth

        -- The edge-on pose is already nearly invisible; the opacity ramp
        -- just hides the sliver of thickness right at the start and end.
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(flipIn * 5.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(foldOut))
    end
end

part.yaw / part.pitch / part.z are script-only 3D fields: they can be

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Orbit Reveal
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Camera-driven reveal (3D). The text itself barely moves --
the CAMERA does the telop work. It starts far around to the left with
strong perspective and pulled back, orbits to a frontal framing while
zooming in and relaxing the lens, then leaves around the OTHER side
while pulling away, like a crane shot passing a signboard.

Camera fields are OnPreLayout-only; the per-character stagger fade in
OnLayout is the only text-side animation.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.4 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kIntroYawDegrees = -65.0 -- camera starts this far around to the left
local kOutroYawDegrees = 55.0 -- camera leaves around the right side
local kIntroPitchDegrees = 14.0 -- slight high angle at the start
local kRestZoom = 1.0
local kIntroZoom = 0.82 -- pulled back at the start
local kOutroZoom = 0.7 -- pulled back further at the end
local kRestPerspective = 0.45
local kAngledPerspective = 0.95 -- lens is widest while the camera is off-axis
local kFadeStagger = 0.4 -- how much of each window is spread across characters

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local arriveEase = mt.ease.in_out_cubic(introAmount)
    local leaveEase = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)

    ctx.camera.yaw = (1.0 - arriveEase) * kIntroYawDegrees + leaveEase * kOutroYawDegrees
    ctx.camera.pitch = (1.0 - arriveEase) * kIntroPitchDegrees
    ctx.camera.zoom = kIntroZoom + (kRestZoom - kIntroZoom) * arriveEase
        + (kOutroZoom - kRestZoom) * leaveEase
    ctx.camera.perspective = kRestPerspective
        + (kAngledPerspective - kRestPerspective) * ((1.0 - arriveEase) + leaveEase)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kFadeStagger
        local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        character.opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
description:
Camera-driven reveal (3D). The text itself barely moves --
the CAMERA does the telop work. It starts far around to the left with
strong perspective and pulled back, orbits to a frontal framing while
zooming in and relaxing the lens, then leaves around the OTHER side
while pulling away, like a crane shot passing a signboard.

Camera fields are OnPreLayout-only; the per-character stagger fade in
OnLayout is the only text-side animation.

-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- @title Stamp Slam
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Characters drop in from just in front
of the camera (z negative = huge) and slam onto the resting plane one
after another on a fixed real-time schedule; every impact kicks the
camera's lens shift with a short decaying shake, so the whole frame
flinches on each hit. At the outro all characters launch back toward
the viewer together.

The slam schedule is index-based real seconds, so OnPreLayout (which
has no char_count) can rebuild the same impact times from ctx.text to
drive the camera shake in sync with OnLayout's drops.
]]

local kFirstSlamDelay = 0.25 -- seconds before the first character starts falling
local kSlamInterval = 0.15 -- seconds between consecutive characters
local kSlamDuration = 0.22 -- seconds each character takes to fall
local kStartDepth = -0.9 -- z at the start of a drop (toward the camera, huge)
local kSettleTiltDegrees = 12.0 -- random tilt while airborne, straightening on impact
local kShakeDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each impact shake takes to die out
local kShakeAmplitude = 0.012 -- lens-shift peak, canvas fraction
local kShakeFrequency = 22.0 -- shake oscillations per second
local kOutroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kExitDepth = -1.2 -- z at the end of the outro launch
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

local function slamLandTime(index)
    return kFirstSlamDelay + (index - 1) * kSlamInterval + kSlamDuration
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- char_count does not exist yet in this hook; the character count is
    -- approximated from the raw text (close enough for the shake window).
    local characterCount = (utf8 and utf8.len(ctx.text)) or #ctx.text

    local shake = 0.0
    for index = 1, characterCount do
        local sinceImpact = ctx.time - slamLandTime(index)
        if sinceImpact >= 0.0 and sinceImpact < kShakeDuration then
            local decay = (1.0 - sinceImpact / kShakeDuration) ^ 2.0
            shake = shake
                + math.sin(sinceImpact * kShakeFrequency * math.pi * 2.0) * decay * kShakeAmplitude
        end
    end

    ctx.camera.lens_shift_x = shake * 0.5
    ctx.camera.lens_shift_y = shake
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local launch = mt.ease.in_cubic(
        mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kOutroDuration))

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local dropStart = slamLandTime(index) - kSlamDuration
        -- Accelerating fall: the stamp hits hardest at the very end.
        local fall = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - dropStart) / kSlamDuration))
        local tilt =
            mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, -kSettleTiltDegrees, kSettleTiltDegrees)

        character.z = (1.0 - fall) * kStartDepth + launch * kExitDepth
        character.rotation = tilt * (1.0 - fall)
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(fall * 4.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(launch))
    end
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title News Flash
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Breaking-news telop. Intro: (1) the bounding box's bottom
edge draws itself left-to-right as an underline, (2) the band fill
lights up behind it, (3) the text slides on while its tracking
converges. Outro reverses the order: text off, band off, then the line
retracts toward the RIGHT edge, completing the left-to-right pen path.

Line-draw technique: a box edge always grows symmetrically from the
bounds center (length = text width + 2 * margin_x). Anchoring one END
of the edge only needs the margin delta:
  left-anchored  growth : stroke_offset_x = margin - kBandMarginX
  right-anchored shrink : stroke_offset_x = kBandMarginX - margin
The zero-length start margin is -textWidth/2 in fontSize percent; the
em size is approximated as (ascent + descent) * canvas height.
]]

local kLineInDuration = 0.5 -- seconds the underline takes to draw
local kBandInDelay = 0.5 -- seconds before the band fill starts lighting
local kBandInDuration = 0.3
local kTextInDelay = 0.75 -- seconds before the text starts sliding on
local kTextInDuration = 0.5
local kTextOutLead = 1.1 -- seconds before clip end the text starts leaving
local kTextOutDuration = 0.35
local kBandOutDuration = 0.25 -- band-off runs right before the line retracts
local kLineOutLead = 0.45 -- the line retracts over the final stretch
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kBandMarginX = 22.0 -- fontSize percent, final underline overhang
local kBandMarginY = 18.0 -- fontSize percent, band height around the text
local kLineWidth = 6.0 -- fontSize percent
local kBandColor = { r = 0.72, g = 0.05, b = 0.11, a = 1.0 }
local kBandOpacity = 0.9
local kTrackingSpread = 0.04 -- extra tracking while the text is still loose
local kSlideDistance = 0.03 -- canvas fraction the text slides in from
local kTextStagger = 0.4 -- entrance cascade across characters

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 0.8
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 45.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.55 }

    local textIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - kTextInDelay) / kTextInDuration))
    ctx.global.tracking = (1.0 - textIn) * kTrackingSpread
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    -- Text bounds width, converted to fontSize percent via the em
    -- approximation, gives the margin at which the edge length is zero.
    local minEdge = math.huge
    local maxEdge = -math.huge
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local geometry = ctx.chars[index].geometry
        minEdge = math.min(minEdge, geometry.bounds_center_x - geometry.bounds_width * 0.5)
        maxEdge = math.max(maxEdge, geometry.bounds_center_x + geometry.bounds_width * 0.5)
    end
    local textWidthPx = math.max(maxEdge - minEdge, 0.0) * ctx.canvas.width
    local fontSizePx = (ctx.font.ascent + ctx.font.descent) * ctx.canvas.height
    local zeroLengthMargin = -textWidthPx / math.max(fontSizePx, 1.0) * 100.0 * 0.5

    local lineIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(ctx.time / kLineInDuration))
    local lineOut = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kLineOutLead))

    local margin
    local lineOffset
    if lineOut > 0.0 then
        -- Right-anchored retraction: the left endpoint sweeps rightward.
        margin = kBandMarginX + (zeroLengthMargin - kBandMarginX) * lineOut
        lineOffset = kBandMarginX - margin
    else
        -- Left-anchored growth: the right endpoint sweeps rightward.
        margin = zeroLengthMargin + (kBandMarginX - zeroLengthMargin) * lineIn
        lineOffset = margin - kBandMarginX
    end

    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = true
    ctx.bounding_box.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.bounding_box.width = kLineWidth
    ctx.bounding_box.start_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.end_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = margin
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = kBandMarginY
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_x = lineOffset

    -- The band fill spans the full final box regardless of the line
    -- animation (margin_x also stretches it, so it is gated by opacity
    -- instead and only lights up after the line has finished drawing).
    local bandIn = mt.saturate((ctx.time - kBandInDelay) / kBandInDuration)
    local bandOut = mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - kLineOutLead) / kBandOutDuration)
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = kBandColor
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = bandIn * (1.0 - bandOut) * kBandOpacity

    local textInAmount = mt.saturate((ctx.time - kTextInDelay) / kTextInDuration)
    local textOutAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kTextOutLead - kTextOutDuration)) / kTextOutDuration)
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kTextStagger
        local slideIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(textInAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local slideOut = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(textOutAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_x = 0.5 - (1.0 - slideIn) * kSlideDistance + slideOut * kSlideDistance
        character.opacity = slideIn * (1.0 - slideOut)
    end
end

The zero-length start margin is -textWidth/2 in fontSize percent; the

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #0f0f1a
-- @title Neon Flicker
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
The fill is transparent so only the neon stroke
"tube" shows; a same-color shadow at zero distance doubles as a cheap
glow. Letters ignite one by one in random order with the erratic
fluorescent flicker of a warming tube, shimmer gently while lit, and at
the outro the power is cut -- everything goes dark except one brief
afterglow blip before the end.

Unlit letters stay faintly visible (a dark glass tube), so the sign's
shape never fully disappears. All flicker is deterministic noise.
]]

local kIgniteWindow = 1.2 -- seconds over which the letters start igniting
local kIgniteDuration = 0.8 -- seconds each letter takes to stabilize
local kFlickerSpeed = 16.0 -- flicker samples per second while warming up
local kShimmerSpeed = 1.4 -- slow brightness shimmer while fully lit
local kPowerCutLead = 0.8 -- seconds before clip end the power dies
local kBlipStart = 0.38 -- afterglow blip window, seconds of remaining time
local kBlipEnd = 0.3
local kUnlitBrightness = 0.06 -- dark-tube brightness when a letter is off
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueA = 340.0 -- oklch hue, pink tubes (odd letters)
local kHueB = 200.0 -- oklch hue, cyan tubes (even letters)

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.transparent = true
    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.012
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 0.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 0.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local igniteDelay = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kIgniteWindow)
        local warmup = mt.saturate((ctx.time - igniteDelay) / kIgniteDuration)

        -- Warm-up flicker: the tube strikes on and off, staying on more
        -- often as warmup approaches 1; then a gentle shimmer while lit.
        local strike = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kFlickerSpeed + index * 7.3, 11)
        local brightness
        if strike > 1.0 - 2.0 * warmup then
            brightness = 0.45 + 0.55 * warmup
        else
            brightness = kUnlitBrightness
        end
        if warmup >= 1.0 then
            brightness = 1.0 - 0.08 * (0.5 + 0.5 * mt.noise1(ctx.time * kShimmerSpeed + index, 12))
        end

        -- Power cut: dark for the rest of the clip, except one shared
        -- afterglow blip.
        if remainingSeconds < kPowerCutLead then
            brightness = kUnlitBrightness
            if remainingSeconds < kBlipStart and remainingSeconds > kBlipEnd then
                brightness = 0.7
            end
        end

        local hue = kHueA
        if index % 2 == 0 then
            hue = kHueB
        end
        local tubeColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.35 + 0.45 * brightness, 0.09 + 0.13 * brightness, hue)

        character.stroke.use = true
        character.stroke.width = 0.012 + 0.004 * brightness
        character.stroke.gap = 0.0
        character.stroke.color = tubeColor
        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = mt.color.with_alpha(tubeColor, 0.55 * brightness)
        character.opacity = 0.3 + 0.7 * brightness
    end
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Gold Shine
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
A warm gold fill carries a near-white
gradient band whose start/end positions sweep across the text on a
fixed period -- the classic specular "shine" pass -- framed by a thin
dark stroke and a soft drop shadow. The entrance is deliberately slow:
tracking converges while the characters fade up; the exit loosens the
tracking again and settles down in place. Elegance over energy.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.4 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kShinePeriod = 2.4 -- seconds between shine passes
local kShineHalfWidth = 0.16 -- gradient-position half width of the shine band
local kShineAngleDegrees = 24.0 -- shine sweeps slightly off-vertical
local kTrackingSpread = 0.05 -- extra tracking while loose
local kRiseDistance = 0.02 -- canvas fraction of the entrance rise
local kFadeStagger = 0.5 -- entrance/exit cascade across characters
local kGoldFill = { r = 0.82, g = 0.66, b = 0.30, a = 1.0 }
local kShineColor = { r = 1.0, g = 0.96, b = 0.82, a = 1.0 }
local kStrokeColor = { r = 0.32, g = 0.23, b = 0.08, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local settleIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount)
    local loosenOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)

    ctx.global.fill.color = kGoldFill
    ctx.global.tracking = (1.0 - settleIn) * kTrackingSpread + loosenOut * kTrackingSpread

    -- Shine pass: a narrow bright band rides the gradient positions from
    -- before the text to past it, once per period, forever.
    local shineCenter = mt.cycle(ctx.time, kShinePeriod) * (1.0 + 2.0 * kShineHalfWidth * 2.0)
        - kShineHalfWidth * 2.0
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab"
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = kShineColor
    ctx.global.gradient.angle = kShineAngleDegrees
    ctx.global.gradient.midpoint = 0.5
    ctx.global.gradient.start_position = shineCenter - kShineHalfWidth
    ctx.global.gradient.end_position = shineCenter + kShineHalfWidth

    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.004
    ctx.global.stroke.color = kStrokeColor
    ctx.global.stroke.order = "fill_over_stroke"
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"

    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.2
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 45.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.05, g = 0.03, b = 0.0, a = 0.35 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kFadeStagger
        local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_y = 0.5 - (1.0 - fadeIn) * kRiseDistance
        character.opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg checkerboard #dddddd
-- @title Jelly Pop
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Rainbow-colored characters drop in one by
one and land with a full squash-and-stretch: stretched long while
falling, squashed flat on impact (bottom-edge pivot so the squash sits
on the baseline), then springing back with an elastic wobble. Each
character's own shadow alpha doubles as a height cue -- faint while
airborne, solid once landed. The outro is a crouch-and-jump straight
up off the screen (in_back supplies the crouch for free).
]]

local kDropWindow = 0.9 -- seconds over which the drops are staggered
local kFallDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each character falls
local kDropHeight = 0.22 -- canvas fraction fallen
local kRecoverDuration = 0.6 -- seconds the squash takes to spring back
local kSquashX = 1.45 -- width multiplier at full squash
local kSquashY = 0.55 -- height multiplier at full squash
local kAirStretchX = 0.85 -- width multiplier while falling
local kAirStretchY = 1.2 -- height multiplier while falling
local kJumpLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the jumps start
local kJumpDuration = 0.5 -- seconds each character takes to leave
local kJumpStagger = 0.4 -- exit cascade across characters
local kJumpHeight = 0.5 -- canvas fraction jumped
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueSpread = 0.9 -- fraction of the hue wheel across the line

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- The per-character shadow colors below only recolor the shadow; the
    -- shadow itself must be enabled globally.
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.4
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 90.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local jumpAmount = mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kJumpLead - kJumpDuration)) / kJumpDuration)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))

        local dropStart = order * kDropWindow
        local fall = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate((ctx.time - dropStart) / kFallDuration))
        local sinceLanding = ctx.time - (dropStart + kFallDuration)
        local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(sinceLanding / kRecoverDuration))

        local stretchX
        local stretchY
        if sinceLanding >= 0.0 then
            stretchX = kSquashX + (1.0 - kSquashX) * recover
            stretchY = kSquashY + (1.0 - kSquashY) * recover
        else
            stretchX = kAirStretchX
            stretchY = kAirStretchY
        end

        local jumpStagger = order * kJumpStagger
        local jump = mt.ease.in_back(mt.saturate(jumpAmount * (1.0 + jumpStagger) - jumpStagger))
        local jumpFade = mt.saturate(jumpAmount * (1.0 + jumpStagger) - jumpStagger)

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - fall) * kDropHeight + jump * kJumpHeight
        character.stretch_x = stretchX
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
        character.opacity = fall * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(jumpFade))

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(order * kHueSpread, 0.72, 1.0, 1.0)
        -- Height cue: the contact shadow only darkens once the character
        -- has actually landed.
        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.1 + 0.35 * fall }
    end
end
