airborne, solid once landed. The outro is a crouch-and-jump straight

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 12
-- @recommend pos 0.5 0.85 bg #aabbcc
-- @recommend text "花鳥風月\n山紫水明"
-- @title Vertical Ink
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
The text is set vertically in top-aligned columns and revealed stroke by
stroke like brush lettering. Each freshly drawn stroke starts as wet, near-black
ink slightly swollen on the page, then dries toward a settled sumi
gray over about a second (mt.color.lerp). The outro is a mist fade:
the columns drift softly upward and dissolve in writing order.

The drying timing uses the part's layout index as an approximation of
its reveal time (same caveat as 05_stroke_order_draw.lua).

The writing rate is fixed real seconds, but if the clip is too short
to finish all strokes before the mist fade, the rate is compressed so
the full text is always written (same pattern as 01_typewriter.lua).
]]

local kSecondsPerStroke = 0.13 -- preferred writing rate, anchored to the clip start
local kFinishedHold = 0.4 -- seconds the completed text should at least hold
local kDryDuration = 1.1 -- seconds a stroke takes to dry
local kWetSwell = 0.07 -- extra scale while the ink is wet
local kMistLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the mist fade starts
local kMistDuration = 0.6 -- seconds each character takes to dissolve
local kMistStagger = 0.5 -- dissolve cascade in writing order
local kMistRise = 0.04 -- canvas fraction drifted upward while dissolving
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kWetInk = { r = 0.04, g = 0.04, b = 0.09, a = 1.0 }
local kDriedInk = { r = 0.22, g = 0.22, b = 0.26, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.h_align = "center"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.15
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local partCount = math.max(ctx.part_count, 1)

    -- Compress the writing rate only when the clip cannot fit every
    -- stroke before the mist fade (plus a short hold on the full text).
    local clipLength = kFallbackClipLength
    if ctx.timeline.available then
        clipLength = ctx.timeline.duration_seconds
    end
    local writingBudget = math.max(clipLength - kMistLead - kFinishedHold, kFinishedHold)
    local secondsPerStroke = math.min(kSecondsPerStroke, writingBudget / partCount)

    local writtenStrokes = mt.clamp(ctx.time / secondsPerStroke, 0.0, partCount)

    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part"
    ctx.output.reorder_parts = true
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = writtenStrokes / partCount

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local sinceDrawn = ctx.time - index * secondsPerStroke
        local dried = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(sinceDrawn / kDryDuration))

        part.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - dried) * kWetSwell
        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(kWetInk, kDriedInk, dried)
    end

    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local mistAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kMistLead - kMistDuration)) / kMistDuration)
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kMistStagger
        local dissolve = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(mistAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + dissolve * kMistRise
        character.opacity = 1.0 - dissolve
    end
end
description:
The text is set vertically in top-aligned columns and revealed stroke by
stroke like brush lettering. Each freshly drawn stroke starts as wet, near-black
ink slightly swollen on the page, then dries toward a settled sumi
gray over about a second (mt.color.lerp). The outro is a mist fade:
the columns drift softly upward and dissolve in writing order.

The drying timing uses the part's layout index as an approximation of
its reveal time (same caveat as 05_stroke_order_draw.lua).

The writing rate is fixed real seconds, but if the clip is too short
to finish all strokes before the mist fade, the rate is compressed so
the full text is always written (same pattern as 01_typewriter.lua).

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Cosmic Dust
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Parts drift in from deep space as motes
of stardust: a slow convergence with a noise wander that dies away as
each mote docks into its glyph. Color slides around the violet-blue-
cyan band of oklch, drifting with both position and time, and a
deterministic sparkle occasionally spikes a mote's lightness and glow
(same-color zero-distance shadow). The outro scatters everything back
into dust along new directions, sparkling harder as it dissolves.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.6 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.3 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.5 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kMinDrift = 0.15 -- canvas fraction, shortest drift-in distance
local kMaxDrift = 0.32 -- canvas fraction, longest drift-in distance
local kWanderAmount = 0.02 -- canvas fraction of the residual noise wander
local kWanderSpeed = 0.8 -- wander cycles per second
local kBaseHue = 265.0 / 360.0 -- normalized oklch hue, violet
local kHueSwing = 70.0 / 360.0 -- swings down toward cyan
local kHueDriftSpeed = 0.12 -- hue cycles per second
local kSparkleSpeed = 5.0 -- sparkle noise samples per second
local kSparkleSharpness = 3.0 -- higher = rarer, sharper glints

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 0.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local stagger = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kStaggerAmount)
        local dock = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local scatter = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        local inAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local outAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 2, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local drift = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 3, kMinDrift, kMaxDrift)

        -- The wander never fully dies during the hold -- stardust floats.
        local loose = math.max(1.0 - dock, scatter)
        local wanderStrength = kWanderAmount * (0.15 + 0.85 * loose)
        local wanderX = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kWanderSpeed + index * 2.13, 31) * wanderStrength
        local wanderY = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kWanderSpeed + index * 2.13, 32) * wanderStrength

        part.offset_x = 0.5 + math.cos(inAngle) * drift * (1.0 - dock)
            + math.cos(outAngle) * drift * scatter + wanderX
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(inAngle) * drift * (1.0 - dock)
            + math.sin(outAngle) * drift * scatter + wanderY

        -- Sparkle: sharpened positive noise, boosted while dissolving.
        local glint = math.max(mt.noise1(ctx.time * kSparkleSpeed + index * 4.7, 33), 0.0)
            ^ kSparkleSharpness
        local sparkle = glint * (1.0 + scatter * 1.5)

        local hue = kBaseHue - kHueSwing
            * (0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(index * 0.7 + ctx.time * kHueDriftSpeed * math.pi * 2.0))
        local dustColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.68 + 0.27 * mt.saturate(sparkle), 0.11, hue)

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = dustColor
        part.shadow.use = true
        part.shadow.color = mt.color.with_alpha(dustColor, 0.35 + 0.45 * mt.saturate(sparkle))
        part.scale = 0.9 + 0.1 * dock + 0.15 * mt.saturate(sparkle)
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(dock * 2.5) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(scatter))
    end
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Glitch
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Parts corrupt in quantized digital cuts:
horizontal tears (strong X snap, slight Y), random stretch, a neon
fill flash with a contrasting stroke, and occasional one-cut dropouts.
The glitch density shapes the whole telop -- the intro materializes
the text OUT of a dense glitch storm (parts flicker as corruption
before they permanently exist), the hold keeps corruption rare, and
the outro ramps the storm back up until the signal cuts to nothing.
A rare whole-frame horizontal jump (sync loss) rides on top.

Everything is derived from quantized time + instance_seed, so each
frame is a deterministic pose and different instances glitch
differently.
]]

local kGlitchFrequency = 12.0 -- cuts per second
local kIntroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds of the materializing storm
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds of the closing storm
local kSignalCutLead = 0.12 -- seconds of dead signal at the very end
local kHoldGlitchChance = 0.06 -- per-part corruption chance per cut while holding
local kStormGlitchChance = 0.75 -- corruption chance at full storm
local kDropoutChance = 0.05 -- per-part one-cut dropout chance while holding
local kTearOffsetX = 0.035 -- canvas fraction of the horizontal tear
local kTearOffsetY = 0.007 -- slight vertical component
local kTearStretchMin = 0.7 -- horizontal stretch range while corrupted
local kTearStretchMax = 1.6
local kSyncLossChance = 0.06 -- whole-frame jump chance per cut
local kSyncLossOffset = 0.02 -- canvas fraction of the frame jump
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Sync loss: the entire frame jumps sideways for single cuts.
    local cut = math.floor(ctx.time * kGlitchFrequency)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5
    if mt.random_range(seed + cut, 1, 0.0, 1.0) < kSyncLossChance then
        ctx.global.position_x = 0.5
            + mt.random_range(seed + cut, 2, -kSyncLossOffset, kSyncLossOffset)
    end
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local cut = math.floor(ctx.time * kGlitchFrequency)

    -- Storm strength: high while materializing, rare during the hold,
    -- ramping back up before the signal dies.
    local introStorm = 1.0 - mt.saturate(ctx.time / kIntroDuration)
    local outroStorm = mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - kSignalCutLead) / kOutroDuration)
    local storm = math.max(introStorm, outroStorm)
    local glitchChance = kHoldGlitchChance + (kStormGlitchChance - kHoldGlitchChance) * storm
    local signalAlive = remainingSeconds > kSignalCutLead

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]

        -- Materialize: each part permanently exists once the intro storm
        -- has decayed past its personal threshold; before that it only
        -- shows up as corruption flashes.
        local materializeThreshold = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 5, 0.0, 0.9)
        local materialized = (1.0 - introStorm) >= materializeThreshold

        local corruptRoll = mt.random_range(seed + cut, index, 0.0, 1.0)
        local corrupted = corruptRoll < glitchChance
        local droppedOut = not corrupted
            and mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, 1.0) < kDropoutChance

        if corrupted then
            part.offset_x = 0.5
                + mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 2, -kTearOffsetX, kTearOffsetX)
            part.offset_y = 0.5
                + mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 3, -kTearOffsetY, kTearOffsetY)
            part.stretch_x =
                mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 4, kTearStretchMin, kTearStretchMax)
            -- Neon flash with a clashing stroke: a cheap chromatic split.
            local flashHue = mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 6, 0.0, 1.0)
            part.fill.use = true
            part.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(flashHue, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
            part.stroke.use = true
            part.stroke.width = 0.005
            part.stroke.gap = 0.0
            part.stroke.color = mt.color.from_hsv(mt.wrap(flashHue + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0, 1.0, 0.9)
        else
            part.offset_x = 0.5
            part.offset_y = 0.5
            part.stretch_x = 1.0
            part.fill.use = false
            part.stroke.use = false
        end

        local visible = corrupted or (materialized and not droppedOut)
        part.opacity = (signalAlive and visible) and 1.0 or 0.0
    end
end

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 2.8
-- @title Brake Pileup
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
The whole line sprints in from off-screen right,
the lead character slams on the brakes at its natural spot and pitches
forward from the sudden stop, and each trailing character keeps running
until it rams the pile, squashing slightly taller on impact. After a short
beat the line relaxes back to its natural spacing and proportions with elasticity.

Modified to be more comical: trailing impacts propagate forward, pushing and
squashing preceding characters further, and the recovery springs back elastically.
Characters now strictly respect physical boundaries and cannot slip past each other.
Running phase features an energetic cartoon-like bounce, a late deceleration (local brake)
right before impact so trailing characters run unaware until the collision, and a squash/stretch cycle.
Impact features a soft sub-frame cushion and phase-rounded ground landing.
Lean angle is held during the crash pile-up and recovers in sync with layout realignment.
]]

local kEntryDistance = 1.1 -- canvas widths traveled before the brake point
local kBrakeTime = 0.7 -- seconds until the lead character halts in place
local kRunLean = -10.0 -- degrees; negative tips the glyph toward screen left (travel direction)
local kRunStretch = 0.15 -- extra horizontal stretch while sprinting
local kBrakeTip = -28.0 -- lead character's forward pitch at the brake moment
local kGapCompression = 0.45 -- compression factor of the piled spacing
local kPileTall = 0.18 -- baseline vertical squash stretch when piled up
local kImpactPunch = 0.08 -- impact stretch factor (subtle/restrained)
local kImpactFrequency = 3.5 -- lower frequency for the initial impact wiggle
local kImpactDamping = 10.0 -- high damping for the initial impact
local kHoldTime = 0.3 -- pause between the last crash and the realignment
local kRecoverDuration = 1.1 -- seconds to ease back into natural layout (longer for elastic settle)

-- Running animation parameters
local kRunFrequency = 16.0 -- step frequency (steps per second)
local kRunJumpHeight = 0.035 -- vertical bounce height
local kRunAngleOsc = 4.0 -- tilt oscillation amplitude while running
local kRunStretchOsc = 0.06 -- stretch oscillation amplitude while running

-- Cushion parameters (preventing single-frame harsh stops)
local kImpactRiseTime = 0.07 -- seconds taken to reach peak squish (soft cushion)
local kTipRiseTime = 0.05 -- seconds taken to reach peak forward lean (preventing 1-frame rotation snap)
local kOvertakeBuffer = 0.07 -- timeline buffer to blend the brake transition
local kLandDecay = 12.0 -- exponential decay rate for soft vertical landing (preventing drop snap)
local kDecelDuration = 0.18 -- seconds of late deceleration right before hitting the pile

local kRunSpeed = kEntryDistance / kBrakeTime -- canvas widths per second

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local leadX = ctx.chars[1].geometry.bounds_center_x

    -- Calculate crash times based on kinematics. Trailing characters have a longer distance
    -- to travel to the pile-up point, so they crash sequentially from front to back.
    local crashTimes = {}
    local pileShifts = {}
    local maxShift = 0.0
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local pileShift = (ctx.chars[index].geometry.bounds_center_x - leadX) * kGapCompression
        pileShifts[index] = pileShift
        crashTimes[index] = kBrakeTime + pileShift / kRunSpeed
        if pileShift > maxShift then
            maxShift = pileShift
        end
    end

    local lastCrashTime = kBrakeTime + maxShift / kRunSpeed
    local recoverStart = lastCrashTime + kHoldTime
    
    -- Elastic recovery easing
    local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(
        mt.inverse_lerp(recoverStart, recoverStart + kRecoverDuration, ctx.time)
    ))

    -- Pass 1: Calculate temporary stretch, rotation, and offset_x / offset_y per character
    local stretchXs = {}
    local stretchYs = {}
    local rotations = {}
    local tempOffsetsX = {}
    local tempOffsetsY = {}

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local crashTime = crashTimes[index]
        local pileShift = pileShifts[index]

        local offsetX
        local offsetY
        local rotation
        local stretchX
        local stretchY

        -- Round total run cycle to the nearest integer multiple of pi so that
        -- the character always lands exactly on the ground (offsetY = 0.5) at the moment of impact.
        local rawSteps = crashTime * (kRunFrequency / math.pi)
        local roundedSteps = math.floor(rawSteps + 0.5)
        local targetRunCycle = roundedSteps * math.pi
        local brakeTimeStart = crashTime - kDecelDuration

        if ctx.time < crashTime then
            -- Sprint phase: sprint at constant speed initially, and apply a late deceleration
            -- (local brake) only when close to the crash point.
            local cycle
            local runStretch = kRunStretch
            
            if ctx.time < brakeTimeStart then
                -- Constant velocity sprint: unaware of the collision ahead
                offsetX = 0.5 + kEntryDistance - kRunSpeed * ctx.time
                cycle = ctx.time * kRunFrequency
                rotation = kRunLean + math.cos(cycle * 2.0) * kRunAngleOsc
                runStretch = kRunStretch + math.sin(cycle * 2.0) * kRunStretchOsc
            else
                -- Late deceleration phase: apply local ease-out quadratic brake to match speed profile
                local u = (ctx.time - brakeTimeStart) / kDecelDuration
                local ease = u * (2.0 - u) -- Out quadratic ease
                
                local xBrake = 0.5 + kEntryDistance - kRunSpeed * brakeTimeStart
                local xTarget = 0.5 - pileShift
                offsetX = mt.lerp(xBrake, xTarget, ease)
                
                -- Decelerate the foot stride cycle as well, aligning with ground phase-rounded end
                local cycleBrakeStart = brakeTimeStart * kRunFrequency
                cycle = mt.lerp(cycleBrakeStart, targetRunCycle, ease)
                
                -- Blend lean angle and stretch down to impact configuration
                rotation = mt.lerp(kRunLean + math.cos(cycle * 2.0) * kRunAngleOsc, kRunLean, ease)
                runStretch = mt.lerp(kRunStretch + math.sin(cycle * 2.0) * kRunStretchOsc, kRunStretch, ease)
            end
            
            offsetY = 0.5 + math.abs(math.sin(cycle)) * kRunJumpHeight
            stretchX = 1.0 + runStretch
            stretchY = 1.0 / (1.0 + runStretch)
        else
            -- Piled phase
            local sinceCrash = ctx.time - crashTime
            offsetX = 0.5 - pileShift
            
            -- Smoothly decay the last running jump bounce height to ground (0.5).
            local lastBounce = math.abs(math.sin(targetRunCycle)) * kRunJumpHeight
            offsetY = 0.5 + lastBounce * math.exp(-sinceCrash * kLandDecay)
            
            -- Hold the forward lean angle during the pile-up phase,
            -- and let it recover dynamically in sync with the physical layout recovery (recover).
            local rise = mt.saturate(sinceCrash / kTipRiseTime)
            local tipAngle = (index == 1) and kBrakeTip or kRunLean
            local baseRotation = tipAngle * rise
            
            -- Cushion the vertical stretch so the squash builds up over a few frames (kImpactRiseTime)
            local impactFactor = (sinceCrash / kImpactRiseTime) * math.exp(1.0 - sinceCrash / kImpactRiseTime)
            local punch = kImpactPunch * impactFactor
            local baseTall = kPileTall * mt.saturate(sinceCrash / kOvertakeBuffer) + punch

            -- Cascading impacts: trailing impacts propagate non-oscillating squeezing force forward
            local extraTall = 0.0
            local extraOffset = 0.0
            local extraRotation = 0.0

            for j = index + 1, ctx.char_count do
                local sinceOtherCrash = ctx.time - crashTimes[j]
                if sinceOtherCrash >= 0 then
                    local dist = j - index
                    local attenuation = 1.0 / (dist * 0.8 + 0.2) -- Attenuate the shock based on distance
                    
                    -- Smooth rise-and-decay impulse envelope for the shock wave
                    local press = (sinceOtherCrash / kImpactRiseTime) * math.exp(1.0 - sinceOtherCrash / kImpactRiseTime)

                    -- Additional vertical squashing is applied to all characters, including the lead
                    extraTall = extraTall + 0.08 * press * attenuation
                    
                    -- The lead character (index == 1) is the heaviest and remains anchored in position/angle
                    if index > 1 then
                        -- Shoved further left (forward)
                        extraOffset = extraOffset - 0.025 * press * attenuation
                        -- Tilted further forward from the shove
                        extraRotation = extraRotation - 6.0 * press * attenuation
                    end
                end
            end

            offsetX = offsetX + extraOffset
            rotation = baseRotation + extraRotation
            
            local tall = baseTall + extraTall
            stretchY = 1.0 + tall
            stretchX = 1.0 / (1.0 + tall)
        end

        stretchXs[index] = stretchX
        stretchYs[index] = stretchY
        rotations[index] = rotation
        tempOffsetsX[index] = offsetX
        tempOffsetsY[index] = offsetY
    end

    -- Pass 2: Boundary clamping with sub-frame cushion to prevent characters from slipping past each other
    local actualXs = {}
    local kOverlapFactor = 0.85 -- Allow slight overlapping for a squashed/packed visual feel

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local geom = character.geometry
        -- Temporary X position by adding offset to natural position
        local tempX = geom.bounds_center_x + (tempOffsetsX[index] - 0.5)

        if index == 1 then
            actualXs[1] = tempX
        else
            local prevGeom = ctx.chars[index - 1].geometry
            -- Consider current physical width scaled by stretch_x
            local curWidth = geom.bounds_width * stretchXs[index]
            local prevWidth = prevGeom.bounds_width * stretchXs[index - 1]
            
            -- Soften physical boundary on impact: momentarily allow a deeper overlap (cushion),
            -- then spring back to the default packed distance (kOverlapFactor).
            local currentOverlap = kOverlapFactor
            local sinceCrash = ctx.time - crashTimes[index]
            if sinceCrash >= 0 then
                local dip = 0.12 * math.exp(-sinceCrash * 6.0) -- Rapidly returns to normal packed state
                currentOverlap = kOverlapFactor - dip
            end
            
            -- Minimum distance for adjacent characters to touch
            local minDist = (curWidth + prevWidth) * 0.5 * currentOverlap
            
            -- Cannot move left of the preceding character's right boundary (prevent overtaking)
            actualXs[index] = math.max(tempX, actualXs[index - 1] + minDist)
        end
    end

    -- Pass 3: Back-calculate offset_x and apply final state values
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        
        -- Back-calculate the clamped offset_x in the piled state
        local clampedOffsetX = actualXs[index] - character.geometry.bounds_center_x + 0.5
        
        -- Blend with recovery easing and apply final transform values
        character.offset_x = mt.lerp(clampedOffsetX, 0.5, recover)
        character.offset_y = mt.lerp(tempOffsetsY[index], 0.5, recover)
        character.rotation = mt.lerp(rotations[index], 0.0, recover)
        character.stretch_x = mt.lerp(stretchXs[index], 1.0, recover)
        character.stretch_y = mt.lerp(stretchYs[index], 1.0, recover)
    end
end

Modified to be more comical: trailing impacts propagate forward, pushing and

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Light Sweep Prism
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
A tilted band of light sweeps across the
text; as it touches each part, the part lifts toward the camera,
flashes white, then settles into a spectral color derived from its
position, as if the light refracted through the glyphs.

Spatial field animation: the driver is each part's signed distance to
the moving band line, computed from part.geometry.canvas_center_x/y in
aspect-corrected world space — parts respond by where they physically
are, not by index, so the light visibly travels *through* characters
rather than jumping glyph to glyph.

The sweep ping-pongs, revealing on the way out and un-revealing on the
way back, so the loop has no visible reset. The lift uses part.z and
reads best under the 3D preset; the accompanying scale bump keeps the
flash legible in 2D as well.
]]

local kSweepPeriod = 5.0 -- seconds for one full out-and-back sweep
local kSweepAngle = math.rad(20.0) -- tilt of the sweep direction from horizontal
local kBandWidth = 0.09 -- gaussian half-width of the light band, world units
local kSweepReach = 0.9 -- world-space distance the band travels past center
local kLiftHeight = 0.25 -- part.z at full flash
local kBaseHue = 0.55 -- resting hue the prism colors are spread around

local function gaussian(distance, width)
    return math.exp(-(distance * distance) / (width * width))
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local aspect = ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio
    local sweepX = math.cos(kSweepAngle)
    local sweepY = math.sin(kSweepAngle)
    local bandPosition = mt.lerp(-kSweepReach, kSweepReach, mt.pingpong(ctx.time, kSweepPeriod))

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local geometry = part.geometry
        local worldX = (geometry.canvas_center_x - 0.5) * aspect
        local worldY = geometry.canvas_center_y - 0.5

        -- Signed distance along the sweep direction: negative once the
        -- band has passed this part.
        local signedDistance = (worldX * sweepX + worldY * sweepY) - bandPosition

        local flash = gaussian(signedDistance, kBandWidth)
        local lit = mt.smoothstep(0.0, 0.1, -signedDistance)

        -- Spectral color: hue fans out with position so neighboring
        -- parts refract into neighboring wavelengths.
        local prismHue = mt.wrap(kBaseHue + worldY * 0.35 + worldX * 0.12, 0.0, 1.0)
        local prismColor = mt.color.from_hsv(prismHue, 0.65, 1.0, 1.0)
        local dimColor = { r = 0.32, g = 0.33, b = 0.38, a = 1.0 }
        local white = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }

        local settled = mt.color.lerp(dimColor, prismColor, lit)

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(settled, white, flash)
        part.z = flash * kLiftHeight
        part.scale = 1.0 + flash * 0.15
    end
end
description:
A tilted band of light sweeps across the
text; as it touches each part, the part lifts toward the camera,
flashes white, then settles into a spectral color derived from its
position, as if the light refracted through the glyphs.

Spatial field animation: the driver is each part's signed distance to
the moving band line, computed from part.geometry.canvas_center_x/y in
aspect-corrected world space — parts respond by where they physically
are, not by index, so the light visibly travels *through* characters
rather than jumping glyph to glyph.

The sweep ping-pongs, revealing on the way out and un-revealing on the
way back, so the loop has no visible reset. The lift uses part.z and
reads best under the 3D preset; the accompanying scale bump keeps the
flash legible in 2D as well.
title: Light Sweep Prism

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @title Focus Flow
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
The line stays wherever the telop is placed while a magnifying focus
runs through it exactly twice: the intro sweep reveals each character
with a pop as it crosses (characters ahead of it do not exist yet),
and the outro sweep wipes them away again behind it. Between sweeps
the line holds still as a plain readable telop with only a micro
rotation drift.

While the focus crosses a character, that character swells (out_back
gives it a small pop past its peak) and mt.layout.reflow reflows
the neighbors around it -- anchored on the focused character at its
own natural spot with baseline = "natural", so the swell pushes
neighbors aside horizontally while the line's position and height
stay rock solid.

Both sweeps run at a fixed real-time rate per character (compressed
only when the clip is too short for two full passes).
]]

local kSecondsPerCharacter = 0.09 -- sweep rate; smaller = snappier
local kSweepPadding = 1.5 -- the sweep starts/ends this many characters off each end
local kMaxSweepClipFraction = 0.4 -- one sweep may occupy at most this clip fraction
local kFocusBoost = 0.45 -- extra scale at the focus center
local kFocusSigma = 1.4 -- gaussian width of the focus, in characters
local kRetypesetTracking = 0.012 -- spacing handed to mt.layout.reflow
local kRevealSoftness = 1.2 -- how tightly appearance hugs the passing focus
local kWiggleDegrees = 1.1 -- micro rotation drift keeping the hold organic
local kWiggleSpeed = 0.8 -- wiggle time scale
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kRestFill = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 } -- resting color of the line
local kFocusFill = { r = 1.0, g = 0.78, b = 0.25, a = 1.0 } -- accent while the focus crosses

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local clipLength = kFallbackClipLength
    if ctx.timeline.available then
        clipLength = ctx.timeline.duration_seconds
    end
    local characterCount = ctx.char_count

    -- Sweep pacing: fixed real seconds per character, compressed only
    -- when two sweeps would not fit in the clip.
    local sweepSpan = characterCount + 2.0 * kSweepPadding
    local secondsPerCharacter =
        math.min(kSecondsPerCharacter, clipLength * kMaxSweepClipFraction / sweepSpan)
    local sweepDuration = sweepSpan * secondsPerCharacter

    -- Focus positions in index space. The intro sweep starts at clip
    -- start; the outro sweep ends exactly at clip end.
    local introFocus = -kSweepPadding + ctx.time / secondsPerCharacter
    local outroFocus = -kSweepPadding + (sweepDuration - remainingSeconds) / secondsPerCharacter

    -- Pass 1: swell, reveal, and wipe. Scale must be final before the
    -- reflow so retypeset sees the true character widths.
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local introDistance = index - introFocus
        local outroDistance = index - outroFocus
        local focus = math.max(
            math.exp(-(introDistance * introDistance) / (kFocusSigma * kFocusSigma)),
            math.exp(-(outroDistance * outroDistance) / (kFocusSigma * kFocusSigma)))

        -- A character exists from the moment the intro focus reaches it
        -- until the outro focus has passed over it.
        local revealed = mt.smoothstep(-kRevealSoftness, 0.0, introFocus - index)
        local wiped = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kRevealSoftness, outroFocus - index)

        character.scale = 1.0 + kFocusBoost * mt.ease.out_quad(focus)
        character.opacity = revealed * (1.0 - wiped)
        character.rotation = mt.wiggle(ctx.time * kWiggleSpeed, 2.5, kWiggleDegrees, 2, index * 10)

        -- Color rides the same focus weight as the swell, so the accent
        -- travels with the magnifier and cools back to the resting color.
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(kRestFill, kFocusFill, focus)
    end

    -- Pass 2: reflow around the line's center character. Using a stable
    -- center anchor prevents discrete jumps when focus shifts across indices.
    local anchorIndex = math.ceil(ctx.char_count / 2)
    ctx.chars[anchorIndex].offset_x = 0.5
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, kRetypesetTracking, {
        mode = "horizontal",
        anchor = anchorIndex,
    })
end

While the focus crosses a character, that character swells (out_back

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6
-- @recommend text "HERE|PULSE!|>"
-- @title Word Pulse
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
A clearly readable emphasized-word heartbeat.

The character indices below assume the recommended text; with any other
text the length guard in OnLayout simply leaves the scene untouched.

The displayed line is:

    HERE|PULSE!|>
         ^^^^^^

"PULSE!" beats as one coherent phrase. The left divider remains fixed,
while the right divider and arrow move aside as the phrase expands. This
makes mt.layout.reflow's partial-layout effect directly visible without
mixing it with per-character phase waves or unrelated motion.
]]

local kWordStart = 6
local kWordEnd = 11
local kLeftDividerIndex = 5
local kRightDividerIndex = 12
local kIntroDuration = 0.45
local kOutroDuration = 0.55
local kFirstHeartbeatTime = 0.9
local kHeartbeatPeriod = 1.55
local kHeartbeatScale = 0.42
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kBaseFill = { r = 0.92, g = 0.95, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kDividerFill = { r = 0.25, g = 0.7, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kWordRestFill = { r = 1.0, g = 0.72, b = 0.18, a = 1.0 }
local kWordBeatFill = { r = 1.0, g = 0.18, b = 0.08, a = 1.0 }

local function pulseWindow(time, startTime, peakTime, endTime)
    local amount = 0.0
    if time >= startTime and time <= endTime then
        if time <= peakTime then
            amount = mt.smoothstep(startTime, peakTime, time)
        else
            amount = 1.0 - mt.smoothstep(peakTime, endTime, time)
        end
    end
    return amount
end

local function heartbeatAmount(time)
    local amount = 0.0
    if time >= kFirstHeartbeatTime then
        local beatTime = (time - kFirstHeartbeatTime) % kHeartbeatPeriod
        local primaryBeat = pulseWindow(beatTime, 0.0, 0.09, 0.3)
        local secondaryBeat = 0.52 * pulseWindow(beatTime, 0.31, 0.39, 0.62)
        amount = math.max(primaryBeat, secondaryBeat)
    end
    return amount
end

local function setPivotToHorizontalOrigin(character)
    local geometry = character.geometry
    character.pivot_x = 0.5 + geometry.canvas_origin_x - geometry.bounds_center_x
    character.pivot_y = 0.5 + geometry.canvas_origin_y - geometry.bounds_center_y
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.vertical = false
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < kRightDividerIndex then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(
            ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local visibility = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount))
    local heartbeat = heartbeatAmount(ctx.time) * visibility
    local emphasizedScale = 1.0 + kHeartbeatScale * heartbeat

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        character.opacity = visibility
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = kBaseFill

        if index == kLeftDividerIndex or index >= kRightDividerIndex then
            character.fill.color = kDividerFill
        end

        if index >= kWordStart and index <= kWordEnd then
            character.scale = emphasizedScale
            character.fill.color =
                mt.color.lerp(kWordRestFill, kWordBeatFill, heartbeat)

            -- Scaling around each glyph's horizontal typesetting origin
            -- keeps the word on a stable baseline.
            setPivotToHorizontalOrigin(character)
        end
    end

    -- Only the emphasized word and its suffix participate. The word's first
    -- character is the fixed anchor, so "HERE|" never moves. The right
    -- divider and arrow visibly absorb the word's changing advance.
    local reflowTargets = {}
    for index = kWordStart, ctx.char_count do
        table.insert(reflowTargets, index)
    end

    local anchor = ctx.chars[kWordStart]
    anchor.offset_x = 0.5
    anchor.offset_y = 0.5
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, {
        targets = reflowTargets,
        anchor = kWordStart,
        mode = "horizontal",
    })
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- @title Calm Breath
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Calm breathing motion for text that stays on screen a
long time. The whole line inhales and exhales on a slow cycle --
a few percent of scale, with a soft brightness swell riding the same
breath -- and a slight per-character phase lag keeps it from feeling
mechanical. Amplitudes are tuned to be clearly alive at a glance
while staying easy to read past.

Everything is driven by ctx.time alone, so the loop is seamless at
any clip length; the intro and outro are plain quiet fades.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kBreathPeriod = 5.0 -- seconds per full breath
local kBreathScale = 0.03 -- scale amplitude of the breath
local kBreathBrightness = 0.1 -- opacity amplitude riding the breath
local kPhaseLag = 0.4 -- radians of per-character lag along the line
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount)
    local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local phase = index * kPhaseLag
        local breath = mt.wave(ctx.time, 1.0 / kBreathPeriod, phase)

        character.scale = 1.0 + breath * kBreathScale
        character.opacity = (1.0 - kBreathBrightness + breath * kBreathBrightness)
            * fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend pos 0.5 0.85 bg #1e1e1e
-- @recommend text "春はあけぼの\nやうやうしろく"
-- @title Vertical Unroll
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Vertical text is revealed like a hanging scroll: a soft front descends
the canvas and characters
appear as it passes their height -- all columns together, since the
front is positional (bounds_center_y), not index-based. Characters
just below the front lag upward a touch, like paper still curled
around the roller. The outro rolls the scroll back up: a second front
rises from the bottom and hides characters beneath it.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kEdgeSoftness = 0.07 -- canvas fraction over which the front feathers
local kCurlLag = 0.015 -- canvas fraction of the upward curl near the front

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.15
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    -- Text extents in canvas space (Y-up), padded so the feathered
    -- fronts fully clear both ends.
    local topEdge = -math.huge
    local bottomEdge = math.huge
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local geometry = ctx.chars[index].geometry
        topEdge = math.max(topEdge, geometry.bounds_center_y + geometry.bounds_height * 0.5)
        bottomEdge = math.min(bottomEdge, geometry.bounds_center_y - geometry.bounds_height * 0.5)
    end
    topEdge = topEdge + kEdgeSoftness
    bottomEdge = bottomEdge - kEdgeSoftness

    -- Unroll front descends from the top; roll-up front climbs from the
    -- bottom (canvas Y grows upward, so descending means decreasing).
    local unrollFront = topEdge
        - mt.ease.in_out_sine(introAmount) * (topEdge - bottomEdge)
    local rollUpFront = bottomEdge
        + mt.ease.in_out_sine(outroAmount) * (topEdge - bottomEdge)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local positionY = character.geometry.bounds_center_y

        local revealed = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kEdgeSoftness, positionY - unrollFront)
        local hidden = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kEdgeSoftness, rollUpFront - positionY)
        if outroAmount <= 0.0 then
            hidden = 0.0
        end

        -- Paper curl: characters right at the front sit a touch high,
        -- easing down as the roller moves past them.
        local frontDistance = positionY - unrollFront
        local curl = math.exp(-(frontDistance * frontDistance)
            / (kEdgeSoftness * kEdgeSoftness)) * kCurlLag

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + curl * (1.0 - mt.saturate(introAmount * 2.0 - 1.0))
        character.opacity = revealed * (1.0 - hidden)
    end
end

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5.5
-- @title Ripple Echo
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
A ring-shaped shockwave expands from
the text's geometric center; each character reacts when the wave front
reaches it -- a brief lift, a scale pop, and a cool-to-warm color flash
-- then settles with a soft after-ripple. Because the driver is each
character's radial distance from the center (not its index), the wave
visibly travels through multi-line layouts as a circle rather than a
left-to-right cascade.

The intro is the first expanding front that "wakes" every glyph; the
idle phase keeps a slower second harmonic for a living surface; the
outro reverses the ring so glyphs sink back into stillness from the
outside in.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds for the first wake front to finish
local kOutroDuration = 0.85 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.5 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kWakeRadius = 0.55 -- canvas units the intro front travels past center
local kWaveSpeed = 0.42 -- canvas units per second of the idle harmonic
local kWaveWidth = 0.07 -- half-width of the ring's gaussian envelope
local kLiftHeight = 0.045 -- canvas-height fraction at peak crest
local kScalePop = 0.22 -- extra scale at the crest
local kIdleAmplitude = 0.55 -- relative strength of the continuous harmonic
local kBaseHue = 0.55 -- cyan resting hue
local kFlashHue = 0.08 -- warm flash hue at the crest

local function gaussian(distance, width)
    return math.exp(-(distance * distance) / (width * width))
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local aspect = ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio

    -- Intro front starts collapsed at the center and expands outward.
    local introFront = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount) * kWakeRadius
    -- Idle harmonic keeps a slow ring pinging forever after the wake.
    local idleFront = mt.cycle(ctx.time, kWakeRadius / kWaveSpeed) * kWakeRadius
    -- Outro front collapses from the outside back to the center.
    local outroFront = (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)) * kWakeRadius

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local geometry = character.geometry
        local worldX = (geometry.bounds_center_x - 0.5) * aspect
        local worldY = geometry.bounds_center_y - 0.5
        local radius = math.sqrt(worldX * worldX + worldY * worldY)

        local introCrest = gaussian(radius - introFront, kWaveWidth)
        local idleCrest = gaussian(radius - idleFront, kWaveWidth) * kIdleAmplitude * introAmount
        local outroCrest = gaussian(radius - outroFront, kWaveWidth) * outroAmount

        -- Characters "wake" once the intro front has passed them, and
        -- fall back asleep as the outro front reclaims them from outside.
        local woken = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kWaveWidth * 1.5, introFront - radius)
        local asleep = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kWaveWidth * 1.5, radius - outroFront)
        local presence = woken * (1.0 - asleep * outroAmount)

        local crest = introCrest + idleCrest + outroCrest
        local lift = crest * kLiftHeight
        -- Outro also gently sinks the whole line so the exit is not only a
        -- ring fade but a physical collapse.
        local sink = outroAmount * 0.03

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + lift - sink
        character.scale = 1.0 + crest * kScalePop
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(presence * 1.15) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount) * 0.35)

        local flash = mt.saturate(introCrest + idleCrest * 0.6)
        local restingColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kBaseHue, 0.35, 0.92, 1.0)
        local flashColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kFlashHue, 0.75, 1.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(restingColor, flashColor, flash)
    end
end
description:
A ring-shaped shockwave expands from
the text's geometric center; each character reacts when the wave front
reaches it -- a brief lift, a scale pop, and a cool-to-warm color flash
-- then settles with a soft after-ripple. Because the driver is each
character's radial distance from the center (not its index), the wave
visibly travels through multi-line layouts as a circle rather than a
left-to-right cascade.

The intro is the first expanding front that "wakes" every glyph; the
idle phase keeps a slower second harmonic for a living surface; the
outro reverses the ring so glyphs sink back into stillness from the
outside in.

name: 23_comet_arc.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- @title Comet Arc
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Comet arc path using mt.path.bezier and mt.path.catmull_rom.
Explicit three-block structure driven by closed-form curves, not
frame-to-frame simulation:
  1. Intro  — each character streaks in along its own cubic Bezier
              (offset-space, neutral 0.5 = natural seat). Rotation
              follows the path tangent so glyphs read as comets, not
              sliding cards.
  2. Steady — a small Catmull-Rom figure-eight patrol around the seat,
              still tangent-aligned, with a cool spectral trail color.
  3. Outro  — a different Bezier exit (new control points, not a
              reverse of the intro) that flings glyphs off-frame.

Control points are in offset units (canvas-normalized displacement;
0.5 is zero motion). See API §10.7. Distinct from orbit_reveal /
vortex_spiral (circular z/spin gags) — this is pure path evaluation.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.2
local kOutroDuration = 0.95
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kStaggerAmount = 0.55
local kSteadyRadius = 0.018 -- figure-eight half-size in offset space
local kSteadyPeriod = 2.8 -- seconds per full idle loop
local kTrailHue = 0.55

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        local stagger = order * kStaggerAmount

        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local introEased = mt.ease.out_cubic(introRaw)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)

        -- Per-glyph wing and height so the cascade fans out.
        local wingSign = ((index % 2) == 0) and 1.0 or -1.0
        local entryLift = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.12, 0.22)
        local entrySide = wingSign * mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount, 0.18, 0.32)
        local exitSide = -wingSign * mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 2, 0.22, 0.38)
        local exitDrop = mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 3, -0.08, 0.12)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Intro: Bezier comet arrival (path progress 0 → 1)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local introP0 = { x = 0.5 + entrySide, y = 0.5 + entryLift }
        local introP1 = { x = 0.5 + entrySide * 0.35, y = 0.5 + entryLift * 0.15 }
        local introP2 = { x = 0.5 - wingSign * 0.04, y = 0.5 - 0.02 }
        local introP3 = { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 }
        local introX, introY, introTangentX, introTangentY =
            mt.path.bezier(introP0, introP1, introP2, introP3, introEased)
        local introRotation = math.deg(math.atan(introTangentY, introTangentX))

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Steady: Catmull-Rom figure-eight around the seat
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local loopProgress = mt.cycle(ctx.time + order * 0.35, kSteadyPeriod)
        local idleWaypoints = {
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 },
            { x = 0.5 + kSteadyRadius, y = 0.5 + kSteadyRadius * 0.55 },
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 },
            { x = 0.5 - kSteadyRadius, y = 0.5 - kSteadyRadius * 0.55 },
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 },
        }
        local idleX, idleY, idleTangentX, idleTangentY =
            mt.path.catmull_rom(idleWaypoints, loopProgress)
        local idleRotation = math.deg(math.atan(idleTangentY, idleTangentX)) * 0.35

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. Outro: different Bezier exit (not intro reversed)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local outroP0 = { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 }
        local outroP1 = { x = 0.5 + exitSide * 0.25, y = 0.5 + 0.06 }
        local outroP2 = { x = 0.5 + exitSide * 0.7, y = 0.5 + exitDrop * 0.4 }
        local outroP3 = { x = 0.5 + exitSide, y = 0.5 + exitDrop }
        local outroX, outroY, outroTangentX, outroTangentY =
            mt.path.bezier(outroP0, outroP1, outroP2, outroP3, outroEased)
        local outroRotation = math.deg(math.atan(outroTangentY, outroTangentX))

        -- Pick the active block pose (do not cross-lerp path samples —
        -- that would leave the curve). Outro wins, then intro, else idle.
        local pathX = idleX
        local pathY = idleY
        local rotation = idleRotation
        if outroEased > 0.0 then
            pathX = outroX
            pathY = outroY
            rotation = outroRotation
        elseif introEased < 1.0 then
            pathX = introX
            pathY = introY
            rotation = introRotation
        end

        character.offset_x = pathX
        character.offset_y = pathY
        character.rotation = rotation
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(introRaw * 2.5) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroRaw))
        character.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - introEased) * 0.2 + outroEased * 0.15

        -- Cool comet trail palette; brighter while still airborne on the arc.
        local airAmount = (1.0 - introEased) + outroEased
        local baseColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kTrailHue + order * 0.08, 0.35, 0.88, 1.0)
        local hotColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kTrailHue - 0.08, 0.55, 1.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(baseColor, hotColor, mt.saturate(airAmount))
    end
end

Comet arc path using mt.path.bezier and mt.path.catmull_rom.
Explicit three-block structure driven by closed-form curves, not
frame-to-frame simulation:
  1. Intro  — each character streaks in along its own cubic Bezier
              (offset-space, neutral 0.5 = natural seat). Rotation
              follows the path tangent so glyphs read as comets, not
              sliding cards.
  2. Steady — a small Catmull-Rom figure-eight patrol around the seat,
              still tangent-aligned, with a cool spectral trail color.
  3. Outro  — a different Bezier exit (new control points, not a
              reverse of the intro) that flings glyphs off-frame.

Control points are in offset units (canvas-normalized displacement;
0.5 is zero motion). See API §10.7. Distinct from orbit_reveal /
vortex_spiral (circular z/spin gags) — this is pure path evaluation.

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- @title Newton's Cradle
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Newton's Cradle (ニュートンのゆりかご). End characters swing
along precise arc paths and collide like steel balls on pendulums,
transferring physical displacement and synchronized color shockwaves through inner characters.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 1.0
local kOutroDuration = 0.9
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0

local kSwingPeriod = 0.35 -- seconds for one swing leg (crisp, snappy pendulum)
local kShockDelayPerChar = 0.012 -- seconds delay per char (12ms for ultra-fast, sharp shockwave)
local kMaxSwingAngle = 35.0 -- degrees of max pendulum swing angle
local kPendulumLength = 0.28 -- normalized arc radius for pendulum motion
local kImpactSquash = 0.25 -- horizontal squash factor upon collision
local kImpactDuration = 0.12 -- sharp recovery duration for impact pulse
local kShockPulseDistance = 0.016 -- horizontal shift for inner shockwave

-- Color palette settings for shockwave propagation
local kBaseHue = 0.58 -- cool cyan/blue resting state hue
local kBaseSat = 0.30
local kBaseVal = 0.88

local kShockHue = 0.08 -- warm orange/gold energy flash hue
local kShockSat = 0.90
local kShockVal = 1.0

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)

    -- Calculate total shockwave travel time across the character line
    local shockTravelTime = math.max(0, characterCount - 1) * kShockDelayPerChar

    -- Complete cycle timeline:
    -- Leg 0: Right Out (duration kSwingPeriod)
    -- Leg 1: Right Return & Impact (duration kSwingPeriod)
    -- Leg 2: Shock R -> L Travel (duration shockTravelTime)
    -- Leg 3: Left Out (duration kSwingPeriod)
    -- Leg 4: Left Return & Impact (duration kSwingPeriod)
    -- Leg 5: Shock L -> R Travel (duration shockTravelTime)
    local cycleTime = 4.0 * kSwingPeriod + 2.0 * shockTravelTime
    local localTime = ctx.time % cycleTime

    -- Keyframe timestamps within full cycle
    local tRightOutStart = 0.0
    local tRightReturnStart = kSwingPeriod
    local tRightImpact = 2.0 * kSwingPeriod
    local tLeftOutStart = 2.0 * kSwingPeriod + shockTravelTime
    local tLeftReturnStart = 3.0 * kSwingPeriod + shockTravelTime
    local tLeftImpact = 4.0 * kSwingPeriod + shockTravelTime

    -- Timestamps for shockwave arrival at ends
    local timeSinceRightImpact = localTime - tRightImpact
    if timeSinceRightImpact < 0.0 then
        timeSinceRightImpact = timeSinceRightImpact + cycleTime
    end

    local timeSinceLeftImpact = localTime - tLeftImpact
    if timeSinceLeftImpact < 0.0 then
        timeSinceLeftImpact = timeSinceLeftImpact + cycleTime
    end

    -- Calculate pendulum angles for left and right ends
    local leftAngle = 0.0
    local rightAngle = 0.0

    if localTime >= tRightOutStart and localTime < tRightReturnStart then
        -- Right end swinging OUT (0 -> +kMaxSwingAngle)
        local progress = (localTime - tRightOutStart) / kSwingPeriod
        rightAngle = kMaxSwingAngle * math.sin(progress * (math.pi * 0.5))
    elseif localTime >= tRightReturnStart and localTime < tRightImpact then
        -- Right end swinging BACK (+kMaxSwingAngle -> 0) -> Strikes at tRightImpact!
        local progress = (localTime - tRightReturnStart) / kSwingPeriod
        rightAngle = kMaxSwingAngle * math.cos(progress * (math.pi * 0.5))
    elseif localTime >= tLeftOutStart and localTime < tLeftReturnStart then
        -- Left end swinging OUT (0 -> -kMaxSwingAngle) - starts PRECISELY when R->L shock arrives!
        local progress = (localTime - tLeftOutStart) / kSwingPeriod
        leftAngle = -kMaxSwingAngle * math.sin(progress * (math.pi * 0.5))
    elseif localTime >= tLeftReturnStart and localTime < tLeftImpact then
        -- Left end swinging BACK (-kMaxSwingAngle -> 0) -> Strikes at tLeftImpact!
        local progress = (localTime - tLeftReturnStart) / kSwingPeriod
        leftAngle = -kMaxSwingAngle * math.cos(progress * (math.pi * 0.5))
    end

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]

        local rotation = 0.0
        local offsetX = 0.5
        local offsetY = 0.5
        local stretchX = 1.0
        local stretchY = 1.0
        local shockIntensity = 0.0

        if characterCount == 1 then
            -- Single character simple back-and-forth pendulum
            local angleNormalized = math.sin(ctx.time * (math.pi / (2.0 * kSwingPeriod)))
            local angle = angleNormalized * kMaxSwingAngle
            local rad = math.rad(angle)
            rotation = angle
            offsetX = 0.5 + kPendulumLength * math.sin(rad)
            offsetY = 0.5 + kPendulumLength * (1.0 - math.cos(rad))
            shockIntensity = math.abs(angleNormalized) * 0.5
        else
            local isLeftEnd = (index == 1)
            local isRightEnd = (index == characterCount)
            local isMiddle = not (isLeftEnd or isRightEnd)

            if isLeftEnd then
                local rad = math.rad(leftAngle)
                rotation = leftAngle
                offsetX = 0.5 + kPendulumLength * math.sin(rad)
                offsetY = 0.5 + kPendulumLength * (1.0 - math.cos(rad))

                -- Impact squash when Left end strikes or is struck by arriving R->L shock
                local sinceHit = timeSinceLeftImpact
                if sinceHit >= 0.0 and sinceHit < kImpactDuration then
                    local progress = sinceHit / kImpactDuration
                    local squash = (1.0 - mt.ease.out_quad(progress)) * kImpactSquash
                    stretchX = 1.0 + squash
                    stretchY = 1.0 - squash * 0.4
                    shockIntensity = math.sin(progress * math.pi)
                else
                    shockIntensity = math.abs(leftAngle / kMaxSwingAngle) * 0.5
                end
            elseif isRightEnd then
                local rad = math.rad(rightAngle)
                rotation = rightAngle
                offsetX = 0.5 + kPendulumLength * math.sin(rad)
                offsetY = 0.5 + kPendulumLength * (1.0 - math.cos(rad))

                -- Impact squash when Right end strikes or is struck by arriving L->R shock
                local sinceHit = timeSinceRightImpact
                if sinceHit >= 0.0 and sinceHit < kImpactDuration then
                    local progress = sinceHit / kImpactDuration
                    local squash = (1.0 - mt.ease.out_quad(progress)) * kImpactSquash
                    stretchX = 1.0 + squash
                    stretchY = 1.0 - squash * 0.4
                    shockIntensity = math.sin(progress * math.pi)
                else
                    shockIntensity = math.abs(rightAngle / kMaxSwingAngle) * 0.5
                end
            elseif isMiddle then
                local distFromLeft = index - 1
                local distFromRight = characterCount - index

                -- Shockwave traveling Right -> Left (after Right Impact at tRightImpact)
                local shockRightTime = timeSinceRightImpact - distFromRight * kShockDelayPerChar
                if shockRightTime >= 0.0 and shockRightTime < kImpactDuration then
                    local progress = shockRightTime / kImpactDuration
                    local impulse = math.sin(progress * math.pi) * (1.0 - progress)
                    offsetX = 0.5 - kShockPulseDistance * impulse
                    stretchX = 1.0 + kImpactSquash * 0.35 * impulse
                    shockIntensity = math.max(shockIntensity, impulse)
                end

                -- Shockwave traveling Left -> Right (after Left Impact at tLeftImpact)
                local shockLeftTime = timeSinceLeftImpact - distFromLeft * kShockDelayPerChar
                if shockLeftTime >= 0.0 and shockLeftTime < kImpactDuration then
                    local progress = shockLeftTime / kImpactDuration
                    local impulse = math.sin(progress * math.pi) * (1.0 - progress)
                    offsetX = 0.5 + kShockPulseDistance * impulse
                    stretchX = 1.0 + kImpactSquash * 0.35 * impulse
                    shockIntensity = math.max(shockIntensity, impulse)
                end
            end
        end

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- Synchronized Color & Luminance Wave
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local baseColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kBaseHue, kBaseSat, kBaseVal, 1.0)
        local shockColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kShockHue, kShockSat, kShockVal, 1.0)

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(baseColor, shockColor, mt.saturate(shockIntensity))

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- Intro / Outro Integration
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        local introStagger = order * 0.25
        local outroStagger = (1.0 - order) * 0.25

        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + introStagger) - introStagger)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + outroStagger) - outroStagger)

        local introEased = mt.ease.out_cubic(introRaw)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)

        local introDropY = (1.0 - introEased) * 0.2
        local outroFlyY = -outroEased * 0.2

        character.pivot_x = 0.5
        character.pivot_y = 0.5
        character.offset_x = offsetX
        character.offset_y = offsetY - introDropY + outroFlyY
        character.rotation = rotation * introEased
        character.stretch_x = stretchX
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(introRaw * 3.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroRaw))
    end
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5.0
-- @recommend lang ja pos 0.5 0.18 bg checkerboard #55616d
-- @title Dialogue Cue
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 3
--[[ @description
Dialogue Cue.

A restrained subtitle treatment for spoken dialogue:
  1. A translucent caption card and a slim speaker cue grow
     upward from the bottom edge of the subtitle block.
  2. Lines resolve quickly with a tiny reading-direction delay, then
     remain completely still for comfortable reading.
  3. When the speaker finishes, the sentence gathers subtly toward its
     final visible character. That last punctuation mark holds for one
     extra beat before the card closes.

The motion is intentionally compact and independent of text length, so
long dialogue and multiline subtitles do not turn into slow typewriter
sequences.
]]

local kIntroDuration = 0.48
local kOutroDuration = 0.58
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0
local kLineRevealDelay = 0.1
local kReadingDirectionDelay = 0.1
local kTextRiseDistance = 0.018
local kIntroStretchY = 0.82

local kCardMarginX = 24.0
local kCardMarginY = 16.0
local kCardOpacity = 0.72
local kCardColor = { r = 0.025, g = 0.035, b = 0.065, a = 1.0 }
local kCueColor = { r = 0.38, g = 0.82, b = 1.0, a = 0.95 }
local kCueWidth = 5.0

local kTextColor = { r = 0.96, g = 0.97, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kOutlineColor = { r = 0.015, g = 0.02, b = 0.04, a = 0.92 }
local kOutlineWidth = 0.012
local kShadowColor = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.72 }
local kShadowDistance = 0.75
local kShadowAngle = 90.0

local kOutroCharacterStagger = 0.2
local kSentenceGather = 0.055
local kPunctuationHoldDelay = 0.48
local kPunctuationPulse = 0.1

local function isWhitespace(text)
    return string.match(text, "^%s+$") ~= nil
end

local function getFinalVisibleCharacterIndex(ctx)
    local finalVisibleCharacterIndex = 0
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        if not isWhitespace(ctx.chars[index].text) then
            finalVisibleCharacterIndex = index
        end
    end
    return finalVisibleCharacterIndex
end

local function measureSubtitleBlock(ctx)
    local minimumEdgeX = 0.5
    local maximumEdgeX = 0.5
    local minimumEdgeY = 0.5
    local maximumEdgeY = 0.5
    local hasVisibleCharacter = false
    local maximumLineIndex = 1

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        maximumLineIndex = math.max(maximumLineIndex, character.line_index)
        if not isWhitespace(character.text) then
            local geometry = character.geometry
            local leftEdge = geometry.bounds_center_x - geometry.bounds_width * 0.5
            local rightEdge = geometry.bounds_center_x + geometry.bounds_width * 0.5
            local bottomEdge = geometry.bounds_center_y - geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
            local topEdge = geometry.bounds_center_y + geometry.bounds_height * 0.5

            if hasVisibleCharacter then
                minimumEdgeX = math.min(minimumEdgeX, leftEdge)
                maximumEdgeX = math.max(maximumEdgeX, rightEdge)
                minimumEdgeY = math.min(minimumEdgeY, bottomEdge)
                maximumEdgeY = math.max(maximumEdgeY, topEdge)
            else
                minimumEdgeX = leftEdge
                maximumEdgeX = rightEdge
                minimumEdgeY = bottomEdge
                maximumEdgeY = topEdge
                hasVisibleCharacter = true
            end
        end
    end

    return {
        minimumEdgeX = minimumEdgeX,
        maximumEdgeX = maximumEdgeX,
        minimumEdgeY = minimumEdgeY,
        maximumEdgeY = maximumEdgeY,
        maximumLineIndex = maximumLineIndex,
        hasVisibleCharacter = hasVisibleCharacter,
    }
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.color = kTextColor
    ctx.global.stroke.width = kOutlineWidth
    ctx.global.stroke.gap = 0.0
    ctx.global.stroke.color = kOutlineColor
    ctx.global.stroke.order = "fill_over_stroke"
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"

    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = kShadowDistance
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = kShadowAngle
    ctx.global.shadow.color = kShadowColor
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local subtitleBlock = measureSubtitleBlock(ctx)
    local finalVisibleCharacterIndex = getFinalVisibleCharacterIndex(ctx)
    local safeCharacterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)

    ------------------------------------------------------------
    -- Caption card: bottom-anchored vertical opening and closing
    ------------------------------------------------------------
    local fontSizePixels = (ctx.font.ascent + ctx.font.descent) * ctx.canvas.height
    local textHeightPixels =
        (subtitleBlock.maximumEdgeY - subtitleBlock.minimumEdgeY) * ctx.canvas.height
    local zeroHeightMargin =
        -textHeightPixels / math.max(fontSizePixels, 1.0) * 100.0 * 0.5
    local cardIntro = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount)
    local cardOutro = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)
    local cardOpenAmount = cardIntro * (1.0 - cardOutro)
    local animatedMarginY = mt.lerp(zeroHeightMargin, kCardMarginY, cardOpenAmount)
    local bottomAnchorOffsetY = kCardMarginY - animatedMarginY

    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = subtitleBlock.hasVisibleCharacter
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = true
    ctx.bounding_box.color = kCueColor
    ctx.bounding_box.width = kCueWidth
    ctx.bounding_box.start_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.end_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = kCardMarginX
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = animatedMarginY
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_y = bottomAnchorOffsetY
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = kCardColor
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = kCardOpacity * cardOpenAmount
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_offset_y = bottomAnchorOffsetY

    ------------------------------------------------------------
    -- Subtitle text: fast line resolve, stable hold, punctuation beat
    ------------------------------------------------------------
    local finalCharacterPositionX = 0.5
    local finalCharacterPositionY = 0.5
    if finalVisibleCharacterIndex > 0 then
        local finalGeometry = ctx.chars[finalVisibleCharacterIndex].geometry
        finalCharacterPositionX = finalGeometry.bounds_center_x
        finalCharacterPositionY = finalGeometry.bounds_center_y
    end

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local geometry = character.geometry
        local characterOrder = mt.distribute(index, safeCharacterCount)
        local lineOrder =
            mt.distribute(character.line_index, subtitleBlock.maximumLineIndex)
        local revealDelay =
            lineOrder * kLineRevealDelay + characterOrder * kReadingDirectionDelay
        local characterIntro = mt.ease.out_cubic(
            mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + revealDelay) - revealDelay)
        )

        local reverseOrder = 1.0 - characterOrder
        local outroDelay = reverseOrder * kOutroCharacterStagger
        local characterOutro = mt.ease.in_quad(
            mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + outroDelay) - outroDelay)
        )

        local punctuationPulse = 0.0
        if index == finalVisibleCharacterIndex then
            characterOutro = mt.ease.in_quad(
                mt.saturate(
                    (outroAmount - kPunctuationHoldDelay)
                        / (1.0 - kPunctuationHoldDelay)
                )
            )
            punctuationPulse =
                math.sin(mt.saturate(outroAmount / kPunctuationHoldDelay) * math.pi)
                    * kPunctuationPulse
        end

        local gatherOffsetX =
            (finalCharacterPositionX - geometry.bounds_center_x)
                * kSentenceGather
                * characterOutro
        local gatherOffsetY =
            (finalCharacterPositionY - geometry.bounds_center_y)
                * kSentenceGather
                * characterOutro

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + gatherOffsetX
        character.offset_y = 0.5
            - (1.0 - characterIntro) * kTextRiseDistance
            + gatherOffsetY
        character.stretch_y = mt.lerp(kIntroStretchY, 1.0, characterIntro)
        character.scale = 1.0 + punctuationPulse
        character.opacity = characterIntro * (1.0 - characterOutro)
    end
end
